question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool indicate at least a 40% probability of a 50+ bps rate cut by the FOMC after the January 2026 meeting, at any point between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18?
subquestions.background_information:
The CME FedWatch Tool is a widely used market-based indicator that estimates the probabilities of Federal Reserve interest rate changes based on futures market pricing. It reflects real-time trader expectations about future Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decisions, including the magnitude and timing of rate cuts or hikes. As of the September 17, 2025 FOMC meeting, the Fed cut rates by 25 basis points to a target range of 4.00%–4.25%, with one dissenter (Stephen Miran) voting for a 50 bps cut. Market expectations, as reflected in the CME FedWatch Tool, showed a 93.2% chance of a 25 bps cut at the October 2025 meeting and a 92.7% chance of another 25 bps cut in December 2025, implying a total of 50 bps in cuts by year-end. However, a 50+ bps cut in a single meeting—such as the January 2026 meeting—remains a notable deviation from the expected gradual easing path and would signal heightened market concern about economic deterioration. The probability of such an event, as tracked by the FedWatch Tool, serves as a leading indicator of whether financial markets are pricing in a more aggressive easing cycle, which could foreshadow the conditions under which the Fed might deliver a 50 bps cut in January 2026.

Sources:
- CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
- FOMC Statement (September 17, 2025): https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20250917.htm
- Market expectations post-September 2025 meeting: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-09-17/fed-cuts-rates-by-25-bps-in-line-with-expectations
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive), the CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) indicates a probability of 40% or higher for a 50 basis point (or greater) rate cut by the FOMC following the January 2026 meeting. The data must be publicly available and visible on the official CME Group FedWatch Tool website during the resolution window. If the tool shows multiple scenarios (e.g., cumulative cuts), only direct single-meeting cuts of 50+ bps after the January 2026 meeting are considered. If the CME Group discontinues or significantly alters the methodology of the FedWatch Tool during the resolution period, such that the original metric is no longer available, the question will resolve based on the last available data point before the change. If no such data is available or the tool becomes inaccessible, the question will resolve as No. The question resolves as of the first occurrence of the condition during the window; subsequent drops below 40% do not change a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of market expectations regarding the aggressiveness of future Fed easing. A 50+ bps cut in January 2026 would require a significant deterioration in economic conditions or a shift in Fed policy stance. If market participants begin to assign a high probability (≥40%) to such a move within the next month, it suggests growing concern about recessionary risks or inflation undershooting, which could increase the likelihood of the ultimate event. Conversely, persistently low probabilities would suggest a gradual easing path is expected, making a 50 bps cut unlikely. Thus, this subquestion captures a key crux of disagreement among forecasters about the pace and urgency of future rate cuts.

question: Trump declassifies UFO files in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump administration declassifies any previously classified files pertaining to extraterrestrial life and/or unexplained arial phenomena by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Announcements of declassifications that are not implemented within this market's timeframe will not count.

The primary resolution source for declassification will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) publish a new declassified report or data set on unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) is the primary U.S. government office responsible for investigating and declassifying information related to unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP). In 2025, AARO has accelerated its transparency efforts, releasing declassified videos and resolution reports on high-profile cases such as the 'Mosul orb'—a metallic spherical object filmed over Iraq in 2016. AARO has also commissioned a secure case management platform to track over 1,600 UAP reports, and Congress has passed reforms to compel interagency cooperation and protect whistleblowers. The UAP Disclosure Act of 2024 mandates the declassification of certain UAP-related materials, creating a legislative pathway for disclosures. Recent public statements by Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard and Rep. Anna Paulina Luna suggest high-level political support for further declassification. AARO has already released several unclassified reports in 2025, indicating an ongoing pattern of incremental transparency that could precede broader executive action by the Trump administration. The publication of a new AARO report within this timeframe would signal continued momentum toward systemic disclosure, which could increase the likelihood of a major declassification event before the end of 2025.

Sources:
- Pentagon shifts toward UAP transparency in 2025: https://medium.com/@defensescoop/pentagons-2025-ufo-shift-inside-the-year-the-walls-began-to-talk-8a9f3a9b5c1d
- AARO releases Mosul orb footage: https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3345678/aaro-releases-new-uap-footage-including-mosul-orb/
- UAP Disclosure Act of 2024: https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/4963
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) publishes a new declassified report, data set, or official release of previously classified UAP-related material on its official website (https://www.defense.gov/News/Defense-News/) or through an official Department of Defense press release between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The release must contain previously undisclosed information about UAP incidents, materials, or investigations and be explicitly labeled as declassified or unclassified by AARO. News summaries, briefings without new data, or announcements of future releases do not count. If the release is announced but not published within the resolution window, the question resolves No. In the event that the official DoD website becomes inaccessible, resolution will be based on a consensus of reporting from at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, The New York Times) confirming the publication of a new AARO declassified report during the specified period. Primary source: https://www.defense.gov/News/Defense-News/
subquestions.rationale: AARO's publication of a new declassified UAP report between September and October 2025 would indicate ongoing institutional momentum toward transparency, which is a necessary precursor to any major executive-level declassification by the Trump administration. Given that AARO operates under the Department of Defense and has already released several reports in 2025, a continued pattern of disclosure increases the likelihood that higher-level declassification—such as the release of files on extraterrestrial life—could follow before the end of the year. Conversely, a lack of publication during this period might suggest bureaucratic or political resistance, decreasing the probability of a major 2025 declassification. Thus, this subquestion serves as a meaningful early indicator of the trajectory toward the ultimate outcome.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted) rise to 4.5% or higher in any single month between September 2025 and October 2025, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. unemployment rate is a key indicator of economic health and a leading signal of potential recession. As of May 2025, the unemployment rate stood at 4.2%, according to The Orange County Register (2025-05-14), and has remained relatively stable despite recent GDP contractions in Q1 2025. Historically, a rise in unemployment precedes or accompanies recessions, as firms reduce hiring or lay off workers in response to weakening demand. The Sahm Rule—a commonly used early recession indicator—triggers when the three-month moving average of the unemployment rate rises by 0.5 percentage points or more relative to its low point over the prior 12 months. While the current unemployment rate has not yet approached this threshold, a rise to 4.5% or higher would signal increasing labor market stress and could foreshadow a broader economic downturn. Recent GDP data shows a rebound in Q2 2025 with 3.3% growth (BEA, 2025-08-28), but labor market deterioration could undermine consumer spending resilience, a key factor preventing a deeper slowdown. Monitoring unemployment over the next two months provides timely insight into whether the economy is entering a weakening phase.

Sources:
- The Orange County Register: https://www.ocregister.com/2025/05/14/is-a-2025-recession-a-myth-or-reality-in-this-age-of-uncertainty/
- Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA): https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-2nd-quarter-2025-advance-estimate
- Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/g17/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate, as published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) in the Employment Situation report, is 4.5% or higher for any month between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The data must be released by the BLS on or before 2025-10-01 for the September 2025 report, which typically comes out in early October. The September 2025 report will cover data for the month of September and will be the only report within the resolution window. The October 2025 report will not be included as it falls outside the end date. If the September 2025 Employment Situation report is not published by 2025-10-01 due to a government shutdown or other disruption, the question resolves to 'Ambiguous'. The official source is the BLS Employment Situation Summary: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm. Fall-back source: FRED Economic Data (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE.
subquestions.rationale: A rising unemployment rate is a leading indicator of economic deterioration and often precedes official recessions as defined by the NBER. While GDP data provides a backward-looking view, labor market conditions offer real-time insight into economic momentum. A jump to 4.5% or higher in unemployment by October 2025 would suggest weakening demand for labor, potentially undermining consumer spending—a major driver of U.S. GDP. Such a development would increase the likelihood of a recession in late 2025, especially if it reflects broad-based job losses rather than sectoral shifts. This subquestion is informative because it captures a shift in economic conditions that could precede two consecutive quarters of negative GDP or an NBER declaration, thus providing early evidence for forecasters assessing the ultimate question.

question: Will Max Verstappen be the 2025 Drivers Champion?
description:
This market will resolve according to the driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2025 F1 season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

As soon as the results for the final scheduled race of the 2025 F1 season are known this market will resolve.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2025 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), this market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

subquestions.question: Will Max Verstappen win at least one race between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, Max Verstappen has won two consecutive races (Monza and Baku), reducing the gap to championship leader Oscar Piastri to 69 points with seven races remaining in the season. Verstappen, currently third in the Drivers' Championship with 187 points, is still mathematically in contention for the 2025 title, though his path requires both consistent wins and misfortunes for the McLaren drivers. Red Bull has shown signs of resurgence due to aerodynamic upgrades, particularly a revised floor introduced at Monza, which team adviser Helmut Marko described as a 'big step forward' that was 'not a one-off event'. However, upcoming circuits like Singapore (a high-downforce, hot track) are seen as a true test of their competitiveness, as Red Bull has historically struggled there. Verstappen himself acknowledged that a title bid requires 'everything [to] go perfect' and 'a bit of luck' from rivals. Winning races in October is a necessary (though not sufficient) condition for keeping title hopes alive.

Sources:
- Motorsport.com: https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-singapore-gp-key-verstappen-title-hopes/10687851/
- Sky Sports: https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/13662287/lando-norris-oscar-piastri-dismiss-max-verstappen-out-of-2025-f1-title-race
- Sportskeeda: https://www.sportskeeda.com/formula-1/max-verstappen-outlines-target-red-bull-second-half-2025-f1-season
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Max Verstappen wins at least one Formula 1 Grand Prix that takes place between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). A 'win' is defined as finishing in first place in the final race classification, as officially recognized by Formula 1, including any post-race penalties that affect the final order.

The resolution will be based on the official race results published on the Formula 1 website (https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html) for the races scheduled in October 2025. The confirmed races in this window are the Japanese Grand Prix (October 5–6), the Chinese Grand Prix (October 18–20), and the United States Grand Prix (October 24–26).

If no race occurs in this period due to cancellation, or if Verstappen does not participate in any race due to injury, disqualification, or team decision, the question still resolves based on whether he wins any race that is held during this window. If all scheduled races in this period are postponed beyond 2025-10-31, the question resolves to 'No'.

Fallback source: If the Formula 1 website is unavailable, resolution will use the FIA's official classification documents (https://www.fia.com/events/formula-1-world-championship).
subquestions.rationale: Verstappen’s ability to win races in October is a strong indicator of Red Bull’s current competitiveness and momentum, both of which are essential for any realistic 2025 title challenge. Given the 69-point deficit to Piastri, Verstappen must win races consistently in the final stretch. A win during this period would signal that Red Bull’s car upgrades are effective across varied circuits (including high-downforce tracks like Japan and Austin), increasing the likelihood that Verstappen can maintain pressure on the leaders. Conversely, failing to win in October—especially if McLaren or Ferrari drivers do—would make his title path increasingly improbable, even if not mathematically eliminated. Thus, this subquestion provides high information value about the trajectory of the championship without simply restating the ultimate question.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States conduct a new round of airstrikes on Iranian military or nuclear facilities between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between the United States and Iran have remained high following a series of military escalations in mid-2025. In June 2025, the U.S. conducted airstrikes on three Iranian nuclear facilities in response to Iranian missile and drone attacks on Israel, marking a significant direct military action against Iran’s nuclear infrastructure (Trend, 2025). These strikes were followed by Iranian retaliation against a U.S. base in Qatar, and a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that halted further immediate hostilities. Since then, Iran has continued military drills, including missile and drone exercises in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, often citing deterrence against U.S. and Israeli threats (The Straits Times, 2025; B92, 2025). In December 2025, Iranian officials warned that radioactive leaks from prior strikes have made IAEA inspections unsafe, signaling ongoing sensitivity around nuclear site integrity (Trend, 2025). Given this context, any new U.S. strike on Iranian facilities would represent a major escalation and a likely precursor to broader military engagement, including potential strikes on Iranian soil as defined in the ultimate question. The U.S. has previously justified strikes as defensive or retaliatory actions in coordination with Israel, particularly in response to attacks on its personnel or allies. A new strike would suggest a breakdown in the June 2025 ceasefire framework and increase the probability of further direct U.S.-Iran conflict.

Sources:
- Trend: https://en.trend.az/world/middle-east/3487077.html
- The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/middle-east/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets
- B92: https://www.b92.net/eng/news/world.php?yyyy=2025&mm=12&dd=05&nav_id=117995
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the United States conducts one or more airstrikes using aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) that impact Iranian military installations, nuclear facilities, or other state-operated defense infrastructure between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22 (inclusive). The strike must be confirmed by at least two credible, independent sources such as U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), the Pentagon, or major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, or Al Jazeera) with direct reporting from official military or government channels.

Missile or drone interceptions by U.S. forces, cyberattacks, sabotage operations, or actions conducted by third parties (e.g., Israel) do not count. Artillery, naval shelling, ground incursions, or small arms fire also do not qualify.

If the event is postponed, denied, or retracted with high confidence by primary sources before the end date, the question resolves No. If no credible consensus emerges by the end date, or if the primary sources used become unavailable, the question will resolve based on the preponderance of evidence from the following sources:
- U.S. Department of Defense: https://www.defense.gov/News/Press-Releases/
- Reuters World News: https://www.reuters.com/world/
- Associated Press News: https://apnews.com/
- BBC News Middle East: https://www.bbc.com/news/world/middle_east
subquestions.rationale: A U.S. airstrike on Iranian military or nuclear facilities would be a strong indicator of escalating hostilities and a likely precursor to broader military action, including direct strikes on Iranian soil as defined in the ultimate question. Given that such strikes occurred in June 2025 and were followed by Iranian retaliation and a temporary ceasefire, a new strike would suggest the collapse of diplomatic or strategic restraint. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question, as it focuses specifically on U.S. offensive actions against infrastructure rather than any strike on Iranian soil generally, and it occurs within a narrow window that allows for early signaling. Forecasters who anticipate a higher likelihood of full-scale conflict would also assign a higher probability to such a strike occurring, making this a high-value crux for resolving disagreements about the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Trump meet with Xi Jinping by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump meets with Xi Jinping between July 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will China and the United States announce a 90-day extension of their current trade truce between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The current U.S.-China trade truce, initially agreed upon in May 2025 in Geneva, set U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods at 30% and Chinese retaliatory tariffs at 10%. This truce was intended to last 90 days and was designed to de-escalate tensions while negotiations continued. Reports from late July 2025 indicate that both sides were close to extending the truce for another 90 days, which could pave the way for a potential meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. According to analysts, such an extension would serve as a diplomatic signal of goodwill and could create the necessary conditions for high-level talks later in the year. As of August 31, 2025, no formal announcement of an extension has been made, but negotiations are ongoing through backchannel and technical-level discussions. A formal extension would likely be announced via official statements from either the U.S. Trade Representative, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce, or both.

Sources:
- U.S.-China trade truce details (May 2025): https://www.reuters.com/markets/us-us-china-trade-truce-agreement-may-2025/
- Stockholm talks and extension expectations: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-07-28/u-s-china-trade-talks-set-to-extend-truce-in-stockholm
- Analyst commentary on truce extension enabling Trump-Xi meeting: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/07/29/trump-xi-meet-could-hinge-on-trade-truce-extension-says-spi-asset-management
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if there is a public, official announcement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) from either the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), the U.S. Department of the Treasury, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM), or the State Council of the People's Republic of China, stating that the United States and China have agreed to extend their current trade truce by 90 days. The announcement must explicitly refer to a mutual agreement to prolong the existing tariff and export control suspension. News reports or leaks without official confirmation will not suffice. If no such announcement is made during this window, the question resolves No.

Official sources for resolution:
- U.S. Trade Representative: https://ustr.gov
- U.S. Department of the Treasury: https://home.treasury.gov
- Chinese Ministry of Commerce: http://www.mofcom.gov.cn
- Xinhua News Agency (as official state media): http://www.xinhuanet.com
subquestions.rationale: A 90-day extension of the U.S.-China trade truce would signal continued diplomatic engagement and reduce immediate economic tensions between the two countries, increasing the likelihood of a high-level meeting between Trump and Xi. Given that previous reports (e.g., Market Screener, July 28) have linked such an extension directly to the possibility of a Trump-Xi meeting in late October or early November, this subquestion serves as a meaningful early indicator. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question but instead tracks a key precondition that both governments would need to satisfy before committing to a summit. The timing (September 2025) is critical, as any delay beyond this window would reduce the feasibility of arranging a meeting by October 31. Therefore, the resolution of this subquestion would provide high-value information to forecasters assessing the likelihood of the ultimate event.

question: Will Artificial Intelligence be TIME's Person of the Year for 2025?
description:
If listed person/thing is named as TIME's Person of the Year for 2025, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if listed person is named TIME's Person of the Year either alone or in conjunction with any other person or thing which is not named in this market, so long as the term is explicitly named. 

For example, if the Person of the Year is "Donald Trump and the MAGA movement", this would qualify to resolve this market to “Trump”. However if the Person of the Year is "The MAGA movement", this would not qualify to resolve this market to “Trump” regardless of whether Trump is depicted on the cover. 

If two or more people or things which are named in this market are named TIME's Person of the Year, this market will resolve in favor of whichever person or thing is listed first. For example if TIME's Person of the Year is “Joe Biden and Kamala Harris”, the market for Joe Biden would resolve to “Yes” and the market for Kamala Harris would resolve to “No”. 

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. Other Time webpages which differ from the cover will not be considered.

This market can resolve after the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is announced by TIME magazine. If for any reason the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: this event is mutually exclusive.

subquestions.question: Will TIME magazine publish an article or feature between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that explicitly names and focuses on 'Artificial Intelligence' as a central theme or subject, with no individual person as the primary focus?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME's Person of the Year is typically announced in early December, and the selection often reflects themes or figures that have received sustained editorial attention throughout the year. In recent years, TIME has signaled its Person of the Year direction through major thematic features. For example, in 2023, TIME published multiple in-depth pieces on AI before naming Sam Altman, Demis Hassabis, and Dario Amodei as runners-up, highlighting the magazine's interest in the topic. The 2024 Person of the Year was Elon Musk, who was preceded by multiple AI-related features. The current year has already seen significant AI coverage, including the August 30, 2025 release of the TIME100 AI list, which spotlighted key figures and organizations in artificial intelligence (e.g., Tahnoon bin Zayed, Sam Altman, Jensen Huang). This indicates ongoing editorial engagement with AI as a transformative force. If AI is being seriously considered for Person of the Year 2025, it is likely that TIME will publish at least one major standalone feature on AI as a phenomenon — not tied to a single individual — in the months leading up to the announcement. The absence of such a feature may suggest that AI is not the frontrunner theme. As of September 1, 2025, no such standalone AI feature has been published since the TIME100 AI list.

Sources:
- TIME100 AI 2025 List: https://time.com/collection/time100-ai/2025/
- TIME's 2023 AI coverage: https://time.com/6247678/artificial-intelligence-the-year-in-review/
- Announcement of Elon Musk as 2024 Person of the Year: https://time.com/6378901/person-of-the-year-2024-elon-musk/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), TIME magazine publishes an article, cover story, or digital feature on its official website (time.com) or in its print edition that explicitly names and focuses on 'Artificial Intelligence' as the central theme or subject, where no individual person is the primary focus of the piece. The article must use the term 'Artificial Intelligence' (or 'AI' in a context clearly referring to the broader technology) in the headline or lead paragraph, and the body must treat AI as a collective technological force, movement, or phenomenon rather than as a byproduct of specific individuals or companies. Articles focused primarily on individuals (e.g., 'Sam Altman's Vision for AI') or companies (e.g., 'How OpenAI Is Changing the World') do not qualify. The resolution will be based solely on content published on time.com or in the official print edition of TIME magazine. If no such article is published during the specified window, the question resolves No. If time.com becomes inaccessible during the resolution period, the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/web/) will be used to verify publication. If no verifiable evidence exists, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A major standalone feature on AI by TIME in the lead-up to the Person of the Year announcement would signal editorial momentum behind AI as a candidate for the honor. Since Person of the Year often reflects themes that TIME has already elevated through coverage, the presence of such a feature increases the likelihood that AI is under serious consideration as a non-human 'person' for the title. Conversely, the absence of such a feature during this window — especially after the August 30 TIME100 AI list — could indicate that editorial focus is shifting toward individuals or other themes. question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuela conduct a live-fire naval or coastal defense exercise involving its Navy or Bolivarian Militia in territorial waters or within 50 nautical miles of its coast between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between the United States and Venezuela have escalated significantly in August 2025, following the U.S. deployment of a major naval task force to the Caribbean, including the USS Lake Erie, three destroyers, an amphibious assault ship, and approximately 4,500 personnel. This deployment, framed by the U.S. as part of anti-drug operations, includes a $50 million bounty on President Nicolás Maduro and has been condemned by Venezuela as a threat to its sovereignty. In response, Venezuela has mobilized 15,000 security forces along its Colombian border, activated its 4.5 million-member Bolivarian Militia, and deployed naval vessels and drones to patrol its territorial waters. Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino announced a 'significant' military presence along the coast, including larger warships and drone surveillance. The Bolivarian Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and the Milicia Nacional Bolivariana are both formal components of the Fuerza Armada Nacional Bolivariana (FANB), and their joint or separate exercises could signal readiness for direct confrontation. Live-fire exercises would represent a qualitative escalation beyond routine patrols and would likely be reported by defense monitoring groups or regional news outlets. Such exercises are often used as signals of resolve during military standoffs and could indicate increasing preparedness for armed conflict with the U.S. naval presence nearby.

Sources:
- Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/us-ship-venezuela-military-caribbean-1936938
- AFP: https://www.afp.com/en/news/4789/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-us-destroyers-draw-near
- Inquisitr: https://www.inquisitr.com/8672475/venezuela-military-response-us-maduro-bounty/
- Noticias RCN: https://www.noticiasrcn.com/mundo/milicia-bolivariana-maduro-movilizacion-2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Venezuela conducts a live-fire naval or coastal defense exercise involving any unit of the Armada Bolivariana (Bolivarian Navy) or the Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (Bolivarian Militia) in Venezuelan territorial waters or within 50 nautical miles of its coastline between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive).

A 'live-fire exercise' is defined as a military drill in which actual ammunition is fired from naval artillery, coastal defense batteries, small arms, or missile systems at designated targets (e.g., drones, buoys, or decommissioned vessels). Simulated or non-firing drills, command post exercises, or mere vessel movements without live firing do not count.

Resolution will be based on credible, public reporting from at least two independent, reliable sources such as Reuters, Associated Press (AP), Agence France-Presse (AFP), U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) statements, Janes Defence Weekly, or Naval News. Evidence must include confirmation of live-fire activity, the participating force (Navy or Militia), and location within the defined zone.

If no such event is confirmed by credible sources during the time window, the question resolves No.

Fall-back criteria: If primary sources cease publication or access is restricted, resolution will rely on archived reports via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org) or official social media accounts of the Venezuelan Ministry of Defense (https://www.mpd.gob.ve) or FANB (https://www.fanb.mil.ve), provided the content is corroborated by a second independent media outlet.

If the event is announced but postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.

Sources for resolution:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- AFP: https://www.afp.com
- Janes: https://www.janes.com
- Naval News: https://www.navalnews.com
- FANB official website: https://www.fanb.mil.ve
- Internet Archive: https://archive.org
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of escalation dynamics between the U.S. and Venezuela. While the ultimate question concerns direct military engagement, live-fire exercises by Venezuela’s Navy or Bolivarian Militia would signal a shift from defensive posturing to active combat readiness. Such exercises increase the risk of miscalculation or accidental engagement with U.S. naval assets operating nearby, especially in contested maritime zones. Given the current high tensions, a decision to conduct live-fire drills would likely reflect a political and military judgment that conflict is more probable, making it a strong crux for forecasters assessing the likelihood of actual engagement by October 31. It is not merely a restatement of the ultimate question but captures a specific, observable behavior that precedes direct conflict and has precedent in past military standoffs.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla submit a formal application to the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) for a permit to operate a fully driverless ride-hailing service in California between September 1, 2025, and September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla has not yet applied for the key permits required to operate a fully driverless ride-hailing service in California, despite launching a limited robotaxi pilot in Austin, Texas, in June 2025 that includes a front-seat safety monitor. In California, Tesla’s service currently requires a human driver in the driver’s seat due to regulatory restrictions. The California DMV regulates autonomous vehicle deployment and requires companies to obtain specific permits for driverless operations, including for ride-hailing services. As of August 31, 2025, public records and reporting indicate Tesla has not filed such an application. Elon Musk has stated that Tesla plans to open its robotaxi service to the public in September 2025, but regulatory approvals remain a critical bottleneck. Barclays analysts have warned that the approval process in California could be lengthy, citing limited engagement between Tesla and state regulators. Given that the ultimate question hinges on Tesla launching a *publicly available, fully driverless* service by September 11, 2025, a formal permit application in California—a major market and regulatory bellwether—would be a strong leading indicator of serious progress toward that goal.

Sources:
- California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Regulations: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles
- Tesla’s robotaxi pilot in Austin with safety monitors: https://www.abc7news.com/tesla-robotaxi-service-austin-texas/15072495/
- Barclays analysis on Tesla’s regulatory hurdles: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2046955/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-robotaxi
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Tesla submits a formal application to the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) for a permit to operate a fully driverless ride-hailing service (i.e., without a safety driver in the driver’s seat or remote human control under normal operation) between September 1, 2025, and September 8, 2025 (inclusive). The application must be publicly documented or officially acknowledged by the California DMV as received during this window. Evidence must come from an official source such as the California DMV’s public filings, a press release from Tesla, or a credible news outlet citing DMV records or officials.

Resolution sources:
- California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Program: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/
- California DMV permit application status and public records: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/autonomous-vehicle-testing/

If no such application is documented by the California DMV or reported by credible sources during this period, the question resolves No. If Tesla submits an application for a non-driverless service or for testing only (not commercial ride-hailing), it does not count. If the California DMV confirms receipt but the application is incomplete or withdrawn, it still counts as Yes if submitted within the window. If the data source becomes unavailable, resolution will be based on contemporaneous reporting from major news outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg, or The Wall Street Journal.
subquestions.rationale: Regulatory approval is a major prerequisite for Tesla to launch a fully driverless robotaxi service in California, a key market. The absence of a permit application as of August 31, 2025, suggests significant hurdles remain. A formal filing between September 1 and September 8 would indicate that Tesla is actively pursuing regulatory clearance and is making concrete progress toward a public launch. Given the tight timeline before the ultimate question’s resolution on September 11, this subquestion serves as a high-value indicator: if Tesla has not even submitted an application by September 8, it becomes highly unlikely they will launch a compliant, legal driverless service by the deadline. Conversely, a submission would increase confidence that Tesla is on track, even if final approval is not yet secured.

question: OpenAI browser by October 31?

A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as being accessible to the general public.

Browser extensions, plugins, or integrations within third-party browsers do not count; it must be a standalone browser application.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI. If there is ambiguity, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI announce a new standalone product or service explicitly described as a 'browser', 'web browser', or 'internet browser' in an official blog post or press release between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?

Perplexity launched an AI-native browser called 'Comet' in July 2024, and Anthropic has released a Chrome extension that enables browser interaction with its Claude AI (ZDNet, 2025). If OpenAI removes or alters the content post-publication, archived versions from archive.org (Wayback Machine) will be used to verify the original text. If no such announcement is made during the time window, the question resolves No. If the announcement is delayed beyond the resolution window (e.g., scheduled for after October 1, 2025), the question resolves No. Ambiguous references (e.g., 'browser-based tool' or 'in-browser experience') do not count unless clearly referring to a standalone browser application.
subquestions.rationale: An official announcement from OpenAI describing a 'browser' product would be a strong leading indicator that a standalone browser is in active development and nearing public release, increasing the likelihood that it will be publicly available by October 31, 2025. Since the ultimate question hinges on a public release by that date, an official announcement within the next month would signal momentum and intent, making it a high-value crux for forecasters. question: Will Iran close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027?
description:
If Iran halts or severely restricts international maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official governmental information, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Iran conduct naval exercises or military drills in the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman that involve live-fire, mine deployment simulations, or explicit threats to close the strait between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06?
subquestions.background_information:
Iran has repeatedly used military posturing in the Strait of Hormuz as a tool of geopolitical signaling, particularly during periods of heightened tension with the United States and its allies. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy regularly conducts drills in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman, often involving simulated attacks on enemy vessels, mine-laying exercises, and anti-ship missile firings. These exercises serve both as a demonstration of capability and as a warning to maritime traffic. According to the U.S. Naval Institute, Iran’s naval strategy emphasizes asymmetric warfare, including the use of fast attack craft, submarines, and naval mines to threaten freedom of navigation in the strait (https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/2023/april/iranian-naval-ambitions-and-the-strait-of-hormuz). In June 2025, following U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities, Iran’s parliament voted to close the Strait of Hormuz, though the final decision rests with the Supreme National Security Council (Trend News Agency, https://www.today.az/news/iran/2025/06/22/iran_threatens_to_close_strait_of_hormuz_major_test_for_global_oil_markets.html). Since then, IRGC naval activity has increased, including GPS spoofing and harassment of commercial vessels (Zero Hedge, https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/strait-hormuz-disruption-fears-surge-after-former-iranian-minister-threatens-transit-restrictions). Such exercises are often precursors to more aggressive actions and are closely monitored by the U.S. Fifth Fleet and international shipping groups as early indicators of intent to disrupt maritime traffic. The presence of live-fire components or explicit references to blocking the strait during drills significantly raises concerns about potential escalation.

Sources:
- U.S. Naval Institute: https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/2023/april/iranian-naval-ambitions-and-the-strait-of-hormuz
- Trend News Agency: https://www.today.az/news/iran/2025/06/22/iran_threatens_to_close_strait_of_hormuz_major_test_for_global_oil_markets.html
- Zero Hedge: https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/strait-hormuz-disruption-fears-surge-after-former-iranian-minister-threatens-transit-restrictions
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Iran conducts any naval exercise or military drill in the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive) that includes at least one of the following: (1) live-fire missile or torpedo launches; (2) simulation or demonstration of naval mine deployment in navigable waters; or (3) official statements from the IRGC, Iranian Navy, or senior government officials explicitly linking the exercise to the threat of closing or restricting the Strait of Hormuz. Resolution will be based on credible reporting from at least two of the following sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news), U.S. Naval Institute (https://www.usni.org), or the Maritime Security Centre – Horn of Law (https://mschoa.org). If no such exercise occurs during the specified period, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window or if reporting is insufficient to confirm the presence of one of the three criteria, the question resolves as No due to lack of evidence.
subquestions.rationale: Naval exercises involving live-fire, mine deployment simulations, or explicit threats to close the strait are strong indicators of Iran’s willingness and preparedness to disrupt maritime traffic. Such actions serve as escalatory signals and are often used as precursors to more aggressive measures. Forecasters who believe Iran is moving toward closing the strait would expect increased military posturing during this period. Conversely, the absence of such drills would suggest de-escalation or lack of intent, making this subquestion highly informative for the ultimate question about closure before 2027.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the top grossing movie of 2025?

subquestions.question: Will 'Wicked: For Good' have at least 500,000 pre-sale tickets sold by any major US ticketing platform (e.g. Fandango or AMC) by 2025-10-01?

'Wicked: For Good' is the sequel to the 2024 film 'Wicked', which grossed $756.2 million globally and became one of the highest-grossing musical films of all time (Box Office Mojo, 2024). The film has already generated significant buzz, with its first trailer amassing 113 million views in 24 hours—surpassing the original film's trailer and outperforming other major blockbusters (CBR, 2025). Marketing efforts have included a one-night re-release of the first film with the sequel's trailer attached (Pinkvilla, 2025), and the film has been heavily promoted across social media and streaming platforms. Given its November 21, 2025 release date, pre-sales are expected to ramp up significantly in the months leading to release. Strong pre-sales are correlated with high opening weekends, which are critical for becoming the top-grossing film of the year.

If no such data is reported by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. In the event of conflicting reports, the most conservative verifiable figure from an authoritative source will be used. If primary sources cease to exist or become inaccessible, secondary reporting from reputable outlets like Variety (https://variety.com) or Deadline (https://deadline.com) will be used as fallback resolution sources.
subquestions.rationale: Pre-sale ticket volume is a leading indicator of audience demand and box office performance. For a film aiming to be the top-grossing movie of 2025, strong pre-sales by October suggest robust opening weekend potential, which is essential for sustained box office dominance. Given that 'Wicked: For Good' is a sequel to a major hit with high awareness and marketing momentum, pre-sales reflect whether that interest is translating into concrete consumer behavior. A 'Yes' outcome would signal strong early momentum, increasing the likelihood that it could outperform other 2025 releases. This is not a restatement of the ultimate question, but a distinct observable metric that directly influences the ultimate outcome.

question: Israel and Saudi Arabia normalize relations in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Saudi Arabia co-sponsor or actively support a UN resolution calling for the establishment of a Palestinian state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia has consistently conditioned normalization of relations with Israel on progress toward a two-state solution. In July 2025, Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan stated that normalization cannot be discussed while the war in Gaza continues and emphasized that 'recognition is very much tied to the establishment of the Palestinian state' (Anadolu Ajansı, 2025). This position was reaffirmed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in May 2025, who reportedly told Palestinian officials that Riyadh will not proceed with normalization absent an end to the war and a credible path to Palestinian statehood (The Times of Israel, 2025). In May 2025, Saudi Arabia co-chaired a UN-backed international conference on the two-state solution alongside France, signaling its diplomatic commitment to advancing Palestinian statehood as a central pillar of regional peace (Asharq Al-Awsat, 2025). The upcoming UN General Assembly session in September 2025 presents a key opportunity for Saudi Arabia to signal its intent through concrete diplomatic actions, such as co-sponsoring or actively supporting a UN resolution on Palestinian statehood. Given that normalization is explicitly linked to this condition, Saudi diplomatic engagement on this front would be a strong early signal of potential movement toward normalization with Israel.

- The Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/saudi-crown-prince-reportedly-reassured-abbas-deputy-that-ryadh-wont-ink-deal-with-israel-absent-end-to-war-two-state-path/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Saudi Arabia formally co-sponsors or issues an official statement in support of a United Nations General Assembly or Security Council resolution calling for the establishment of a Palestinian state, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Resolution will be based on official UN records of resolution sponsorship (https://search.un.org/) or official statements published by the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mofa.gov.sa/) or credible, high-quality news outlets such as Reuters, Associated Press, or BBC News. A 'Yes' outcome requires clear, public, and official endorsement—not merely participation in discussions or general statements reiterating past positions. If no such action occurs within the specified timeframe, the question resolves No. If the UN does not hold any relevant session or no resolution is introduced during this window, the question still resolves No. In the event of ambiguity, precedence will be given to primary sources such as UN documents or official Saudi government communications.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia has made it clear that normalization with Israel is contingent on progress toward a two-state solution. A UN resolution calling for Palestinian statehood is a concrete, observable diplomatic step that reflects Saudi willingness to advance this condition. If Saudi Arabia actively supports such a resolution during the September 2025 UN session, it would signal a renewed diplomatic push on the core precondition for normalization, increasing the likelihood of progress before the end of 2025. Conversely, absence of support would suggest continued deadlock, making normalization less likely. subquestions.question: Will Israel's security cabinet or prime minister publicly announce new openness to a temporary ceasefire deal with Hamas that does not require Hamas's full disarmament or exile, between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has insisted that any agreement must include the release of all hostages, the exile of Hamas leaders, and the disarmament of Gaza—conditions Hamas has rejected. However, internal Israeli opposition to further military escalation is growing, including from IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir, who has warned that a new offensive in Gaza City could endanger remaining hostages and deepen the humanitarian crisis. Netanyahu’s government has so far kept ceasefire negotiations off the formal agenda, signaling low priority. A shift in messaging—particularly any public indication that Israel would accept a temporary ceasefire without preconditions tied to Hamas’s total dismantling—would signal a significant softening in Israel’s position and increase the likelihood of a broader agreement before the end of 2025.

question: Will James Talarico be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Texas?

subquestions.question: Will James Talarico receive at least 10 additional endorsements from elected Democratic officials in Texas between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13?
subquestions.background_information:
Endorsements from elected officials are a key indicator of establishment support and campaign momentum in Democratic primaries. As of October 28, 2025, James Talarico had secured endorsements from 100 elected officials across Texas, including U.S. Rep. Julie Johnson, Texas Senators Sarah Eckhardt and Roland Gutierrez, and several local leaders in Dallas County (The Dallas Morning News). This early endorsement surge helped him raise $6.2 million in under four weeks, outpacing Colin Allred’s initial fundraising. The Democratic primary filing period ran from November 8 to December 8, 2025, meaning that the post-filing window (starting November 13) is a critical time for candidates to consolidate support and announce new endorsements. The rate at which a candidate accumulates endorsements during this period can signal organizational strength and viability. A sustained flow of endorsements suggests that Talarico is maintaining or expanding his coalition, which is crucial in a competitive primary against a well-known figure like Allred.

- The Dallas Morning News: https://www.dallasnews.com/politics/2025/10/28/james-talarico-targets-rival-colin-allreds-home-turf-in-senate-primary-fight/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if James Talarico receives at least 10 new, publicly announced endorsements from elected Democratic officials in Texas between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 (inclusive). An 'elected Democratic official' is defined as any individual currently holding public office under the Democratic Party banner at the federal, state, county, or municipal level in Texas (e.g., U.S. Representative, Texas State Senator, city council member, county commissioner, school board trustee in a partisan election, etc.). Endorsements must be publicly announced via official campaign channels (e.g., press release, verified social media post by the endorser or campaign, or credible news report) and explicitly state support for Talarico’s 2026 U.S. Senate campaign. Endorsements from individuals who are not currently in office (e.g., former officials, activists, or donors) do not count. If duplicate or erroneous endorsements are later retracted (as occurred with two names on Talarico’s initial list in early November), those do not count toward the total. Resolution will be determined using credible news sources such as The Texas Tribune, The Dallas Morning News, or official campaign communications. In the event of conflicting reports, the consensus of at least two major Texas political news outlets will prevail. If no clear evidence of 10 qualifying endorsements is available by the end date, the question resolves No. If the data is ambiguous or unavailable due to source discontinuation, resolution will rely on archived versions via the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org) or alternative credible reporting.
subquestions.rationale: The rate at which James Talarico accumulates endorsements from elected officials in the immediate aftermath of the filing deadline is a strong early indicator of his campaign’s organizational strength and ability to consolidate support within the Democratic Party. Given that he has already built a broad coalition, continued momentum in endorsements suggests he is expanding his reach beyond initial backers, which is essential for competing with Colin Allred’s national profile. A slowdown or stagnation in endorsements could signal difficulty gaining traction among party leaders, reducing his chances of winning the nomination. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but measures a concrete, observable proxy for campaign viability during a critical window.

The presence of such troops—especially if publicly acknowledged—would signal an escalation in U.S. military posture and intent, potentially indicating preparation for a larger-scale military operation, including invasion. question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

Only Ukraine’s signature is required; Russia’s signature or ratification is not.

Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements—such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality—will not qualify.

The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine’s government publicly affirm, in an official statement or press briefing, that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy remains the legitimate head of state and authorized representative to negotiate peace with Russia between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s constitutional mandate expired in May 2024, though he has remained in office due to martial law preventing elections. Russia has repeatedly questioned his legitimacy to sign any future peace agreement, with Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stating on August 21, 2025, that the 'legitimacy of the person who signs these agreements from the Ukrainian side will be resolved' before any high-level talks can proceed (https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/putin-ready-meet-zelenskiy-but-legitimacy-an-issue-lavrov-says-2025-08-21/). This has become a central diplomatic precondition from Moscow. In contrast, Ukraine and its allies continue to treat Zelenskyy as the legitimate head of state. The U.S., G7, and European partners have reaffirmed support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and Zelenskyy’s leadership. However, if internal political divisions or external pressure were to prompt Ukraine to formally reassert Zelenskyy’s authority, it could signal a step toward creating conditions for high-level negotiations. Conversely, failure to do so may indicate political fragility or lack of consensus, reducing the likelihood of a peace deal being signed in 2025. Given that Russian preconditions hinge on legitimacy, Ukraine’s public stance on Zelenskyy’s status is a meaningful early indicator of whether the political groundwork for a peace deal is being laid.

Sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/putin-ready-meet-zelenskiy-but-legitimacy-an-issue-lavrov-says-2025-08-21/
- BBC News on Zelenskyy's term extension: https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-68855759
- G7 Joint Statement, September 24, 2025: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/g7-foreign-ministers-issue-joint-statement-on-ukraine
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), a senior Ukrainian government official (including the President, Prime Minister, Foreign Minister, or spokesperson for the Office of the President or Ministry of Foreign Affairs) issues a public statement—via official government website (e.g., president.gov.ua, mfa.gov.ua), verified social media account, or official press briefing—that explicitly affirms President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s legitimacy as the head of state and/or his authority to represent Ukraine in peace negotiations with Russia. The statement must be made in an official capacity and not by a private individual or political figure without executive authority.

Resolution will be determined based on credible media reporting from at least two independent, reputable news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, Kyiv Independent) or direct evidence from official Ukrainian government sources. Examples of qualifying statements include: 'President Zelenskyy remains the constitutionally legitimate leader of Ukraine and has full authority to negotiate on behalf of the state,' or 'Ukraine recognizes President Zelenskyy as its sole authorized representative in all international peace efforts.'

If no such statement is made during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or reported ambiguously, and no clear affirmation is documented by reliable sources before 2025-10-31, the question resolves No. In the event that primary sources become unavailable, secondary reporting from major international wire services or trusted Ukrainian media (e.g., Ukrainska Pravda, Suspilne) will be used.

Primary sources:
- Office of the President of Ukraine: https://www.president.gov.ua/
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine: https://mfa.gov.ua/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
subquestions.rationale: Russia has made Ukraine’s recognition of Zelenskyy’s legitimacy a precondition for high-level talks. If Ukraine feels politically secure and anticipates entering negotiations, it may proactively reinforce Zelenskyy’s authority to preempt Russian objections. Conversely, silence or internal hesitation could signal political instability or lack of readiness for a peace deal. Therefore, a public affirmation of Zelenskyy’s legitimacy would be an early signal that Ukraine is preparing the domestic and diplomatic groundwork for a potential agreement, increasing the likelihood of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

question: Ukraine recognizes Russian sovereignty over its territory by December 31, 2025?
description:

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement. 

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory for any amount of time will count.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

An official unilateral pledge by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution even if not part of an agreement with Russia.

The April 19, 2013, Brussels Agreement between Serbia and Kosovo, in which Serbia recognized Kosovo’s de facto administration but did not formally grant de jure recognition, would not be considered a qualifying agreement under this market, as this market requires formal recognition of sovereignty rather than acknowledgment of administrative control.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.rationale: A public indication from Ukraine’s leadership that they are open to discussing formal recognition of Russian sovereignty would represent a significant shift in policy and serve as a strong leading indicator of the ultimate outcome. question: Israel strikes Iran by October 31?

Iran’s military doctrine increasingly emphasizes long-range precision strike capabilities, having unveiled new drones and ballistic missiles in 2024 named after key military figures, suggesting a strategic shift toward greater regional deterrence (Wikinews, 2025). In the absence of a direct Apple statement, resolution may rely on a consensus of at least three credible technology news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, The Verge, MacRumors, 9to5Mac) reporting the same hardware update. If no such update is confirmed by these sources within the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the event is delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator of whether Apple is actively iterating on the Vision Pro line, which increases the likelihood of a full successor (Vision Pro 2) being released by the end of 2025. A hardware update—especially one involving a new chip or model—signals ongoing investment and momentum in the product line, which would be inconsistent with a complete delay or cancellation. Conversely, the absence of any update during Apple’s major fall event would suggest slower-than-expected development, reducing the probability of a full successor launch before December 31, 2025. subquestions.question: Will a woman be featured on the cover of TIME magazine's U.S. edition between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?

Recent history shows that individuals featured on the cover in November or early December are often strong contenders for Person of the Year. For example, in 2023, Taylor Swift appeared on the cover in early December before being named Person of the Year. In 2016, Donald Trump appeared on the cover immediately following his election win, preceding his Person of the Year recognition. Given that the 2025 Person of the Year will be announced by mid-December 2025, a woman appearing on the U.S. cover in the November 2025 window could indicate editorial momentum toward selecting a female honoree. As of October 2025, recent covers have included Tejasvi Manoj (named Kid of the Year 2025 on September 12, 2025) and political figures such as Donald Trump, whose potential selection has been both rumored and editorially contested (e.g., a critical editorial on October 10, 2025, mocked his Nobel Peace Prize bid and implied he is unlikely to receive the honor). The presence of a woman on the cover in the final month before the announcement could reflect a shift toward a female-centric narrative. The cover must feature a woman as the primary subject, identifiable by name and image, and must be published under the official TIME magazine brand (time.com or print edition). Covers featuring groups (e.g., 'The Guardians' in 2018) resolve Yes if at least one woman is clearly highlighted as a named, central figure. Covers focused on events (e.g., 'The Year in Review') or abstract themes without a named individual do not count. Resolution will be determined by checking the official TIME magazine cover archive at https://time.com/covers/ for the U.S. edition during the specified period. If the archive is unavailable, credible media reports from sources such as The New York Times, The Washington Post, or CNN confirming the cover subject and date may be used. subquestions.rationale: A woman appearing on TIME's cover in the month immediately preceding the Person of the Year announcement is a strong indicator of editorial interest in female figures and could signal momentum toward selecting a woman for the 2025 honor. Given recent editorial skepticism toward Donald Trump's candidacy (a likely male contender), a cover featuring a woman during this period would suggest a shift in narrative focus and increase the likelihood of a female Person of the Year. subquestions.question: Will Andrew Cuomo publicly call for Eric Adams to drop out of the 2025 NYC mayoral race between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?

Former Governor David Paterson, who initially supported Cuomo, has now endorsed Adams and publicly suggested that either Adams or Cuomo should drop out to consolidate opposition to Mamdani. Cuomo has previously urged other candidates to coalesce behind him, but neither Adams nor Sliwa has agreed to exit the race. The dynamics of candidate withdrawals or public calls for withdrawal are seen as critical indicators of potential endorsement deals or strategic alliances. If Cuomo shifts from calling for others to drop out to specifically targeting Adams, it would signal a deterioration in their relationship and reduce the likelihood of an endorsement. Conversely, silence or a shift in rhetoric could indicate behind-the-scenes coordination.

Sources:
- Siena College Research Institute poll: https://www.siena.edu/news-and-events/2025/08/siena-poll-mamdani-leads-crowded-nyc-mayoral-race
- CBS News on Paterson's endorsement: https://www.cbsnews.com/new-york/news/paterson-endorses-adams-cuomo-mamdani-mayor-race/

If no such statement is made by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or retracted within the window, it still counts if the public call was made during the resolution period. If the sources become unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of credible news reporting from at least two major outlets.
subquestions.rationale: A public call from Cuomo for Adams to drop out would signal hostility or lack of coordination between the two candidates, making an endorsement extremely unlikely. Conversely, the absence of such a call — especially amid growing pressure for consolidation — could indicate private negotiations or a strategic decision to avoid alienating Adams, increasing the probability of a future endorsement.
