subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between 2025-09-12 and 2025-10-12 (inclusive), the green trend line for Donald Trump's approval rating on the Silver Bulletin page (https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin) shows an approval rating of 44.0% or higher. The value must be visible and recorded in the publicly accessible trend line as of the date in question. If the Silver Bulletin becomes unavailable during this period, the fallback source is RealClearPolitics' Trump approval average (https://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/latest_polls/president/), and the question resolves Yes if their daily average reaches or exceeds 44.0% at any point in the same window. If neither source publishes data for the entire period and no archived version is available via Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org), the question resolves as Ambiguous. subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator because sustained approval at or above 44.0% in the short term increases the likelihood that Trump will remain within the 44.0–45.9% band by year-end. Given the political inertia in presidential approval ratings and the absence of major scheduled shocks in late 2025, current momentum is a strong predictor of future levels. A failure to reach 44.0% in this window would suggest weakening support, making the ultimate outcome less likely. Thus, this crux captures a key inflection point in the trajectory toward the December 31 measurement.

subquestions.question: Will Maria Margarita Rojas enter a plea deal that includes an admission of guilt on any charge related to providing illegal abortions between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-29?

She is the first individual charged under Texas’s Human Life Protection Act, which bans nearly all abortions except to prevent death or serious physical impairment. The case has drawn national attention, with the Center for Reproductive Rights calling it a 'sham' and arguing that Rojas provided lawful care to low-income, uninsured immigrant families. Her attorney, Nicole DeBorde Hochglaube, has maintained her innocence and criticized Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton for inflammatory public statements. As of October 2025, Rojas had pleaded not guilty, and the case was proceeding toward trial. Plea negotiations are common in high-profile criminal cases and could serve as an early indicator of the likelihood of a conviction at trial. A plea deal with an admission of guilt would strongly suggest that the prosecution has compelling evidence and that a guilty verdict is more likely, while the absence of such a plea may indicate ongoing legal resistance and uncertainty about the outcome.

Conversely, the absence of such a plea by January 2026 suggests that the defense is proceeding to trial, introducing greater uncertainty about the outcome. question: Will the Bank of Canada announce a 25 bps decrease at the March meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the target for the overnight rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Bank of Canada's March 2026 meeting.

If the target for the overnight rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points and will resolve to the relevant bracket. For example, if the deposit facility rate is increased or decreased by 12.5 basis points, it will be treated as a 25 basis point change for the purposes of resolution.

The resolution source for this market is information released by the Bank of Canada after its March 18, 2026 policy meeting, as listed on the official Bank of Canada calendar: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/#target-dates

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Canada's statement for their March meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the Bank of Canada's 3-year bond yield decrease by at least 10 basis points between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bank of Canada's monetary policy decisions influence government bond yields, particularly in the 2- to 5-year range, which are sensitive to expectations about future rate changes. As of December 23, 2025, the Bank held its policy rate steady at 2.25%, with Governing Council stating it was 'about the right level' to maintain inflation near 2% (Bank of Canada, December 2025). However, uncertainty remains about the next policy move, with minutes indicating that 'the next rate move could be either a hike or a cut' depending on incoming data (Bank of Canada, 2025-12-23). Market expectations are a key driver of bond yields. Currently, money markets are pricing in a 25 bps rate hike by October 2026, but a shift toward expectations of a March 2026 cut would likely push bond yields downward. The 3-year Government of Canada bond yield is a widely watched indicator of medium-term rate expectations and is closely correlated with the central bank's policy path. As of December 23, 2025, the 3-year bond yield was approximately 2.45% (Bank of Canada Fixed Income Data). A decline of at least 10 bps in this yield during late December 2025 to mid-January 2026 would signal growing market confidence that the Bank of Canada will cut rates in March 2026, reflecting a shift in market pricing toward easing.

Sources:
- Bank of Canada: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2025/12/monetary-policy-report/
- Bank of Canada Fixed Income Yields: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/selected-bond-yields/
- Market Screener (BoC minutes): https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Bank-of-Canada-can-t-tell-if-next-rate-move-will-be-a-hike-or-a-cut-say-minutes-48948178/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the yield on the 3-year Government of Canada benchmark bond decreases by at least 10 basis points between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23, inclusive. The yield must be lower on any trading day within the period (2025-12-24 to 2026-01-23) compared to the closing yield on 2025-12-23. The closing yield data will be sourced from the Bank of Canada's Selected Bond Yields dataset, specifically the '3-year' column under 'Government of Canada benchmark bond yields'.

Resolution source: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/valet/observations/f10488y/csv

If the Bank of Canada discontinues publication of this data, a fallback source will be the 3-year Canadian government bond yield as reported by Bloomberg (ticker: CB3YR) or Refinitiv Eikon (RIC: CAN3YR=), using end-of-day values. If no reliable data is available by the end date, the question will resolve as 'No'.

This question resolves based on data observed between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23.
subquestions.rationale: Changes in the 3-year government bond yield reflect market expectations about future monetary policy. A decline of at least 10 bps during this window would indicate that investors are increasingly pricing in a rate cut at the March 2026 meeting, serving as an early signal of shifting sentiment. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether the Bank announces a 25 bps cut in March 2026, movements in forward-looking financial indicators like bond yields provide valuable insight into evolving market consensus. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but captures a real-time, observable proxy for expectations, making it a high-value crux for forecasters.

subquestions.question: Will the number of Google searches for 'pregnancy test' in the United States, as measured by Google Trends, have an average weekly index value above 75 between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-16?
subquestions.background_information:
Search interest in terms like 'pregnancy test' can serve as an early behavioral indicator of fertility intentions and activity. While the CDC's fertility data is based on official birth records and lags by several months, digital behavior such as search trends can provide real-time signals about changes in reproductive behavior. Google Trends data has been used in public health research to predict outcomes such as influenza outbreaks and mental health trends (see: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-020-00363-3). The baseline value of 100 in Google Trends represents the peak popularity of the term during the selected time period and geography; a value of 75 would indicate relatively high interest compared to the historical baseline. As of mid-2025, the average weekly index value for 'pregnancy test' in the U.S. has fluctuated between 60 and 70, based on recent 12-month data (https://trends.google.com/trends/explore?date=today%2012-m&geo=US&q=pregnancy%20test). A sustained increase above 75 could signal rising pregnancy-related concerns or attempts, which may precede an increase in fertility rates. This makes it a potentially informative leading indicator for short-term fertility trends.

Sources:
- Nature Digital Medicine on Google Trends and public health: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-020-00363-3
- Google Trends data for 'pregnancy test' in the U.S.: https://trends.google.com/trends/explore?date=today%2012-m&geo=US&q=pregnancy%20test
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the average weekly Google Trends index value for the search term 'pregnancy test' in the United States is above 75 for the period between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-16, inclusive. The data must be retrieved from Google Trends (https://trends.google.com) using the default settings for 'Web Search' and 'United States', with the time range set to '2025-09-01 to 2025-09-16'. The average is calculated by downloading the weekly index values via the 'Download' button in Google Trends and computing the arithmetic mean of all weekly data points in the period. If Google Trends data is unavailable for this period by 2025-09-17, or if the service is down or altered in a way that prevents reliable measurement, the question resolves to 'No'. Adjustments due to sampling or scaling by Google are accepted as published.
subquestions.rationale: Search behavior related to pregnancy testing is a leading indicator of fertility activity. An increase in searches for 'pregnancy test' suggests more individuals are testing for pregnancy, which could precede a rise in the fertility rate. Since the ultimate question concerns whether the U.S. fertility rate will increase in Q2 2025, observing elevated search interest in early September 2025—shortly after the end of Q2—can provide early evidence of sustained reproductive activity that may have contributed to a higher fertility rate. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but captures a behavioral precursor that could help forecasters update their beliefs about the likelihood of a fertility uptick.

subquestions.question: Will Apple announce or confirm the release of AirTag 2 during the September 2025 Apple event?
subquestions.background_information:
Apple is widely expected to hold its annual fall product launch event in early September 2025, likely on September 9 or 10, where it is anticipated to unveil the iPhone 17 series and potentially other accessories. Multiple credible sources, including Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, 9to5Mac, and CNET, have reported that the AirTag 2 is 'nearly ready' and likely to be introduced during this event. The original AirTag was released in April 2021 at $29 for a single unit and $99 for a four-pack, and while the AirTag 2 is expected to include internal upgrades—such as a second-generation Ultra-Wideband (UWB) chip, improved Precision Finding up to 60 meters, and a tamper-proof speaker—its design is expected to remain largely unchanged. Rumors suggest Apple is addressing privacy concerns related to misuse for stalking by making the speaker harder to disable. An official announcement of the AirTag 2 would signal Apple’s commitment to the product line and could provide early clues about its pricing strategy, especially if Apple positions it as a premium update or a cost-optimized successor. Given that the ultimate question hinges on whether AirTag 2 launches under $30, an official announcement in September would be a strong leading indicator that the product is entering final release planning, with pricing likely already determined.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publish the October 2025 Consumer Price Index (CPI) report by October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Consumer Price Index (CPI), published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), is a key inflation indicator and one of the reports covered under the ultimate question’s definition of payroll and labor-related data. The October 2025 CPI report is scheduled for release on October 15, 2025, as part of the BLS's regular publication calendar. According to the BLS’s 2025 contingency plan for a government shutdown, 'Economic data that are scheduled to be released during the lapse will not be released,' and 'all active data collection activities for BLS surveys will cease' during a funding lapse. A shutdown beginning October 1, 2025, would directly threaten the timely release of this report. The CPI is critical not only for Federal Reserve policy decisions but also for the Social Security Administration’s annual Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA). Delays or cancellations of the CPI report would signal a breakdown in BLS operations and could foreshadow a broader cessation of data publication. Given that a government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, this subquestion tests whether BLS maintains its ability to publish high-priority reports despite operational disruptions.

Sources:
- BLS Contingency Plan (2025): https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/OASP/media/organization/bls/BLS%20Contingency%20Plan%202025.pdf
- CPI Release Schedule: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm
- Social Security COLA Impact: https://www.ssa.gov/newsroom/articles/2024/cost-of-living-2025.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes the October 2025 Consumer Price Index (CPI) report on or before October 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. The report must be publicly available on the official BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/) in its standard format, including headline CPI, core CPI, and detailed component data. This question resolves No if the report is not published by that time. A delay announcement posted on the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/) or a news release from the U.S. Department of Labor confirming the cancellation or indefinite postponement of the report during the resolution window (October 1, 2025, to October 15, 2025) will also result in a No resolution. If a preliminary or partial report is published but full data is not released by October 15, the question resolves No. Fall-back source: In the event the BLS website is inaccessible, resolution will be based on official press releases from the U.S. Department of Labor (https://www.dol.gov/newsroom) or consensus reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, Reuters, Bloomberg) confirming publication or non-publication of the report by the deadline.
subquestions.rationale: The timely publication of the October 2025 CPI report is a strong indicator of whether the BLS is maintaining its core data publication functions during a potential government shutdown. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether BLS ceases regular publication of key reports, observing whether a high-profile, scheduled release like CPI occurs as planned provides early evidence of institutional continuity or breakdown. A failure to publish CPI by its scheduled date would suggest that the BLS is unable to resume operations quickly after a shutdown, increasing the likelihood of broader cessation. Conversely, on-time publication would signal resilience and reduce the probability that BLS will cease reporting altogether by the end of 2025.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will the President of the Brazilian Senate, Rodrigo Pacheco, publicly state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that he will schedule a vote on the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, five Brazilian senators from the Liberal Party, led by Congressman Hélio Lopes, have initiated the 30th impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, citing abuse of authority, censorship, and violations of constitutional rights. The move follows U.S. sanctions against Moraes under the Global Magnitsky Act, which some lawmakers argue undermine his legitimacy. However, previous impeachment requests have stalled, largely due to the discretion of Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco, who controls the legislative agenda and whether such motions proceed to a formal vote. As of July 30, 2025, Pacheco had declined to hold an impeachment vote, despite pressure from right-wing factions planning mass protests on September 7. His public statements are seen as a key gatekeeping signal: if he commits to scheduling a vote, it would significantly increase the likelihood of the Federal Senate eventually taking up the impeachment. Pacheco’s position is politically sensitive—he must balance institutional stability with pressure from Bolsonaro-aligned lawmakers. A public commitment to schedule a vote would represent a major shift in momentum toward impeachment.

- Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/world/2025/08/07/brazil-impeach-judge-bolsonaro-house-arrest/
- NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7XJ4Z6Z6YJZ5Z6Z6Z6Z6Z6Z6Z/
- Devdiscourse: https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/2968730-high-stakes-diplomacy-brazilian-judge-in-trump-s-crosshairs
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the President of the Brazilian Senate, Rodrigo Pacheco, makes a public statement—via official Senate communications, press conference, verified social media account (e.g., X @PresidenteSenado or his personal @RodrigoPacheco), or credible news outlet—indicating that he intends to schedule or has scheduled a vote on the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The statement must clearly express intent to move forward with a formal Senate vote, not merely acknowledge receipt of a request or express openness to discussion.

Resolution sources:
- Official Senate website: https://www12.senado.leg.br/
- Rodrigo Pacheco’s verified X account: https://twitter.com/RodrigoPacheco
- Reputable Brazilian news outlets such as G1, Folha de S.Paulo, or Reuters Brasil: https://g1.globo.com/, https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/, https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil/

If no such statement is made by the end date, the question resolves No. If the statement is made but later retracted or contradicted, the resolution is based on the initial public statement. If the data source becomes unavailable, resolution will rely on a consensus of at least two credible, independent news reports confirming or denying the statement.
subquestions.rationale: The President of the Senate holds decisive procedural power over whether impeachment proceedings advance to a vote. His public commitment to scheduling a vote would be a strong indicator that the political threshold for impeachment has been crossed, especially given that 29 prior attempts have failed to gain traction. This subquestion captures a meaningful early signal of institutional momentum toward impeachment, distinct from the ultimate outcome. It is informative because forecasters who believe impeachment is unlikely may still assign higher probability to this event if political pressure intensifies, while those who see it as inevitable would expect Pacheco to act. The timing aligns with planned right-wing protests on September 7 and follows U.S. sanctions, making it a plausible window for a public stance.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US conduct a military strike on a country other than Syria between January 13, 2026, and February 12, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of January 11, 2026, the United States conducted a series of airstrikes in Syria targeting Islamic State locations in response to a December 2025 attack that killed two U.S. soldiers and one civilian interpreter in Palmyra. These strikes involved over 90 bombs and missiles launched from multiple aircraft, including F-15Es, A-10s, AC-130Js, and MQ-9 Reapers, with Jordanian F-16s providing support. This marks the only confirmed U.S. military strike on foreign soil in early 2026. The U.S. maintains approximately 1,000 troops in Syria under Operation Inherent Resolve, though the Pentagon has signaled a gradual drawdown. No other U.S. military strikes have been reported since January 11. However, recent geopolitical tensions—such as the January 3, 2026, U.S. operation in Venezuela that resulted in the capture of President Nicolás Maduro—raise concerns about potential unilateral military actions. While that operation involved ground forces and was not an aerial strike on sovereign soil in the traditional sense, it demonstrates a willingness by the current U.S. administration to conduct high-risk military operations abroad without congressional authorization. Other potential flashpoints include India-Pakistan tensions, Russia-Ukraine escalation involving hypersonic missiles, and instability in the Sahel and Horn of Africa. Given that the ultimate question hinges on whether the U.S. will strike three different countries in 2026, and one strike (in Syria) has already occurred, the likelihood of reaching three depends on whether additional strikes occur in new locations. A strike outside Syria would signal a broader pattern of military engagement and increase the probability of multiple strikes across different nations.

Sources:
- US airstrikes hit Islamic State targets across Syria after attack (OpIndia): https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-syria-islamic-state/
- Pentagon Official on Venezuela War: 'Following the Old, Failed Scripts' (The Intercept): https://theintercept.com/2026/01/05/venezuela-maduro-capture-us-military/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike—defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by U.S. military forces that impact another country's ground territory—on any country other than Syria between January 13, 2026, and February 12, 2026 (inclusive).

Strikes must be officially acknowledged by the U.S. government or confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting. Missile or drone interceptions that do not result in impact on foreign soil do not count. Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or operations by ground operatives without aerial bombardment do not qualify.

Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from at least two of the following sources:
- U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) official statements: https://www.centcom.mil/
- Department of Defense (DoD) news releases: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- Associated Press (AP) reporting: https://apnews.com
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news

If no such strike is confirmed by these sources within the specified time frame, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window or reporting is inconclusive due to source unavailability, the question resolves as 'Ambiguous'.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will strike three different countries in 2026. One strike has already occurred in Syria as of January 11, 2026. This subquestion isolates whether a second distinct strike—outside Syria—occurs in the near term. If the U.S. conducts another strike in a new country within this window, it significantly increases the likelihood that the threshold of three countries will be reached by year-end, especially given the demonstrated willingness to use military force unilaterally. Conversely, a lack of additional strikes suggests a more restrained posture, making it less likely that two more distinct strikes will occur. Thus, this subquestion serves as a high-value indicator of the trajectory toward the ultimate outcome, capturing early momentum in U.S. military engagement patterns for 2026.

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a preliminary injunction blocking Donald Trump from removing a Federal Reserve Governor between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 25–28, 2025, President Donald Trump announced the removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged false statements on mortgage applications as 'cause' under the Federal Reserve Act. Cook rejected the removal, asserting that the president lacks legal authority to fire her without a clear showing of inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance occurring during her tenure. She filed a lawsuit challenging the action, with a hearing scheduled before U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb on August 30, 2025. The outcome of this legal challenge could set a precedent for future presidential attempts to remove Fed officials. Section 10 of the Federal Reserve Act allows removal 'for cause,' but this has historically been interpreted narrowly. A preliminary injunction would temporarily block Cook’s removal and could signal judicial skepticism of Trump’s authority, potentially deterring further removal attempts. If the court denies the injunction, it may embolden Trump to target other governors, such as Chair Jerome Powell or other board members not aligned with his push for lower interest rates. The legal battle is widely seen as a critical test of the Federal Reserve’s independence from political interference.

Sources:
- CNN: https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/politics/trump-fed-governor-lisa-cook-fired/index.html
- The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/trump-fires-lisa-cook-escalating-his-war-on-the-federal-reserve
- Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-blocked-110000234.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a federal court (U.S. District Court or higher) issues a preliminary injunction between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that explicitly blocks President Donald Trump from removing any Federal Reserve Governor, including Lisa Cook, from office. The injunction must be formally issued and publicly available via official court records or a credible news source reporting on the court’s order.

Resolution sources:
- U.S. Courts PACER system (https://pacer.uscourts.gov) for official court documents
- Reuters Legal (https://www.reuters.com/legal)
- Bloomberg Law (https://news.bloomberglaw.com)
- Associated Press (https://apnews.com)

If no such injunction is issued during the specified period, the question resolves No. If the case is dismissed, postponed, or the court declines to rule before the end date, the question still resolves No. In the event that primary sources become unavailable, secondary reporting from at least two major U.S. news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, The Washington Post, Reuters) confirming the issuance of an injunction will be used as fallback resolution criteria.
subquestions.rationale: The issuance of a preliminary injunction would signal strong judicial pushback against Trump’s authority to remove Fed governors, likely discouraging further removal attempts before October 31. Conversely, the absence of such an injunction could indicate legal vulnerability of Fed governors, increasing the likelihood that Trump will attempt to remove another. This makes the court’s action a high-value indicator of whether Trump will escalate his campaign to reshape the Fed leadership, beyond the already contested case of Lisa Cook.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration announce any formal negotiations or bilateral talks with Canada aimed at reducing or eliminating U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, the Trump administration has significantly escalated trade tensions with Canada by eliminating the de minimis exemption for shipments under $800 and raising tariffs on certain Canadian goods not covered by USMCA from 25% to 35%. These actions have disrupted cross-border e-commerce, particularly affecting small businesses in British Columbia and other provinces that rely on U.S. sales. The Canadian government has responded by removing retaliatory tariffs on USMCA-covered goods but maintains tariffs on steel, aluminum, and autos. Despite these tensions, no public negotiations have been announced to roll back U.S. tariffs on Canada. Given the political sensitivity of trade policy and the administration’s stated goal of maximizing tariff revenue, any move toward formal talks would signal a potential shift in stance and could precede actual tariff reductions. Historically, public announcements of bilateral trade negotiations have often preceded executive or legislative action on tariffs, making such a signal a meaningful early indicator of potential de-escalation. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) and the White House are the primary sources for official announcements regarding trade negotiations.

Sources:
- Global News: https://globalnews.ca/news/11542978/duty-free-shipping-to-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses-fearful/
- Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB): https://www.cfib-fcei.ca/en/media/media-releases/bc-small-businesses-impacted-us-tariff-changes
- Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR): https://ustr.gov
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the Trump administration publicly announces formal negotiations or bilateral talks with Canada specifically aimed at reducing or eliminating U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods. The announcement must come from an official source such as the White House, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Department of Commerce, or the U.S. Trade Representative, and must be reported by at least two major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, CBC, or BBC) within 48 hours.

Evidence must clearly state that the purpose of the talks includes reducing or eliminating U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports. Mere diplomatic engagement, routine consultations, or discussions on unrelated trade issues (e.g., energy, border security) do not qualify.

If the announcement is later retracted or canceled, the question still resolves based on whether the announcement was made within the specified time frame.

In the event that the primary source (e.g., USTR website) becomes unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from at least two major news outlets.

Primary resolution source: USTR announcements (https://ustr.gov) and White House press briefings (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/)
Secondary sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com), CBC News (https://www.cbc.ca/news)
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of the ultimate question because formal negotiations between the U.S. and Canada on tariff reductions would strongly suggest a political willingness by the Trump administration to de-escalate trade tensions. Given that no such talks are currently known to be underway, an announcement would represent a significant shift in policy direction and increase the likelihood of actual tariff reductions before the ultimate question’s resolution date. The absence of such talks, conversely, would suggest continued trade hostility and reduce the probability of unilateral tariff relief. Because negotiations typically precede executive or legislative action, this crux helps forecasters update their beliefs about the likelihood of tariff reductions without waiting for the final outcome.

question: Will Microstrategy's mNAV dip to 1.00 by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will MicroStrategy issue new common shares for cash between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
MicroStrategy (now operating under the name 'Strategy') has historically raised capital to purchase Bitcoin through a mix of preferred shares, convertible debt, and at-the-market (ATM) equity issuances. A key factor influencing its market-to-net asset value (mNAV) is the dilution caused by issuing new common shares. In August 2025, the company revised its capital issuance policy, removing its previous pledge not to issue shares when mNAV is below 2.5×, except to cover dividend obligations or when 'deemed advantageous' to the company (CryptoSlate, 2025). This change increases the risk of dilution, especially as mNAV has declined from over 3.4× in late 2024 to approximately 1.5× by September 2025 (CoinDesk, 2025). The company faces $588.7 million in annual preferred dividend obligations (Yahoo! Finance, 2025), while its annualized revenue is only $450 million, creating a cash flow shortfall. If the company issues new common shares to raise cash, this would further dilute existing shareholders and likely exert downward pressure on mNAV. Given that mNAV is already near 1.5×, additional dilution could accelerate the path toward mNAV reaching 1.00 by the end of 2025. Monitoring new equity issuance in October 2025 provides a direct signal of whether the company is taking actions that could destabilize its mNAV trajectory.

Sources:
- CryptoSlate: https://cryptoslate.com/strategy-eases-mstr-stock-sale-limits-as-shares-hit-lowest-level-since-april/
- CoinDesk: https://www.coindesk.com/business/2025/09/08/mstr-news-strategy-acquires-another-1955-btc-for-217m-after-missing-out-on-sp-500-inclusion/
- Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/strategys-dividend-obligations-top-580-120000123.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if MicroStrategy (Strategy) issues new common shares for cash between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). Resolution will be based on official SEC filings, specifically Form 4 (for insider transactions) and Form 8-K (for material events), as published on the SEC's EDGAR database at https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.html. A 'Yes' resolution requires clear disclosure of a new issuance of common stock (ticker: MSTR) for cash consideration, excluding any conversions of preferred shares (e.g., STRK) into common stock, dividend reinvestment plans, or employee stock option exercises unless those result in a net new share issuance beyond existing plans. If no such filing is made by November 15, 2025, and no credible public announcement (e.g., press release or verified executive statement) confirms an issuance during the period, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or announced after the resolution window, it does not count. In the event that SEC filings are unavailable or ambiguous, secondary confirmation from reputable financial news sources such as Bloomberg, Reuters, or The Wall Street Journal will be used.
subquestions.rationale: Equity issuance is a key driver of dilution, which directly reduces mNAV. The ultimate question hinges on whether mNAV reaches 1.00 by the end of 2025. Given that mNAV has already declined from over 3.4× to around 1.5× in 2025, further dilution via share issuance would accelerate the decline. If MicroStrategy issues new common shares in October 2025, it signals a willingness to dilute shareholders even at low mNAV levels, increasing the likelihood that mNAV continues to fall toward 1.00. Conversely, refraining from issuance suggests management may be attempting to stabilize or support mNAV, reducing the probability of hitting 1.00. Thus, this subquestion is a high-value indicator of management's capital strategy and its impact on mNAV trajectory.

question: Will Drake's next album debut No.1 on Billboard 200?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Drake’s next officially released album debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart for its first charted week following release. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Drake does not release a new album by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

This market may resolve as soon as Billboard publishes the first chart week in which the album appears.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from Billboard (https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/).

subquestions.question: Will Drake announce an official release date for his album 'Iceman' between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08?
subquestions.background_information:
Drake's next solo album, tentatively titled 'Iceman', has been highly anticipated since mid-2025, with multiple hints and promotional activity suggesting a late 2025 release. As of October 2025, no official release date has been confirmed, though Drake has been touring in Europe with PARTYNEXTDOOR and promoting new music, including the collaborative album '$ome $exy $ongs 4 U', which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in May 2025 (HotNewHipHop, May 17, 2025). Drake has teased the album on social media and in interviews, stating it's 'coming soon' and describing it as 'a slap' (HotNewHipHop, May 17, 2025; PEOPLE.com, July 5, 2025). Given the typical lead time between album announcement and release in the music industry—often 2–6 weeks—an official date announcement in October or early November would strongly suggest a release before the ultimate question’s cutoff of December 31, 2025. Without such an announcement, the likelihood of a timely release diminishes, especially considering the need for marketing, physical distribution, and chart eligibility.

Sources:
- HotNewHipHop - Drake & PARTYNEXTDOOR's 'Some Sexy Songs 4 U' Surpasses Staggering Sales Milestone: https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/974825-drake-partynextdoor-some-sexy-songs-4-u-platinum
- PEOPLE.com - Drake Appears to Call Out Friends: https://people.com/music/drake-new-song-what-did-i-miss-kendrick-lamar-beef/
- HotNewHipHop - Drake Sends Odd Message About 'Good Times': https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/983675-drake-iceman-album-tour-good-times-message
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08, Drake or an official representative (e.g., OVO Sound, Republic Records, or Drake’s verified social media accounts) announces a specific release date for his upcoming solo album 'Iceman'. The announcement must include a calendar date (e.g., 'November 15, 2025') and be made via a public, verifiable channel such as Instagram, X (Twitter), YouTube, or an official press release.

Resolution sources:
- Drake’s verified Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/drake/
- Drake’s verified X (Twitter): https://twitter.com/drake
- Republic Records official website: https://www.republicrecords.com/artists/drake/
- Billboard news: https://www.billboard.com/artist/drake/

If multiple announcements occur, the first one during the resolution window determines the outcome. If the announcement is later retracted or contradicted, the question still resolves based on the initial public statement. If the album is released during the window without a prior date announcement, the question resolves No. If no such announcement is made by 2025-11-08, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: An official release date announcement is a strong leading indicator of whether Drake’s next album will be released in time to chart before the ultimate question’s deadline of December 31, 2025. Given industry norms, albums are typically announced 2–6 weeks before release to allow for marketing and distribution. A confirmed date within this subquestion’s window would significantly increase the probability that the album is imminent and thus capable of debuting at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Conversely, the absence of such an announcement would suggest delays or uncertainty, reducing the likelihood of both release and chart success. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but a measurable precursor event that directly influences its feasibility.

question: Half-Life 3 released in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Half-Life 3 or a differently titled game continuing the Half-Life series is officially released in the US by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Valve Corporation.

subquestions.question: Will Valve post an official teaser trailer for Half-Life 3 on its YouTube channel between 2025-11-10 and 2025-11-20?
subquestions.background_information:
There is growing speculation in late 2025 that Valve may finally announce Half-Life 3, a game long anticipated by fans since the unresolved cliffhanger of Half-Life 2: Episode Two in 2007. Multiple fan theories and insider reports, including those from Tyler McVicker of the HLX Files podcast, suggest that a trailer for Half-Life 3 is in production and could be released in November 2025. Notably, anomalies in Steam's event calendar—such as the absence of major sales or promotions between November 18 and December 8—have fueled speculation that Valve is reserving this window for a major announcement. The date November 18, 2025, is particularly significant as it marks the sixth anniversary of the announcement of Half-Life: Alyx, a game that reinvigorated the franchise and hinted at a broader narrative continuation. Given Valve's history of tightly controlled marketing and surprise reveals, the release of an official teaser trailer would be a strong signal that a full release of Half-Life 3 is imminent. Valve's YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@ValveSoftware) is the primary platform for official game announcements and trailers, including for titles like Half-Life: Alyx and Portal 2.

Sources:
- Eurogamer: https://www.eurogamer.net/half-life-fans-believe-theyve-worked-out-a-possible-announcement-date-for-half-life-3-and-its-very-very-soon
- gamereactor.eu: https://www.gamereactor.eu/half-life-3-trailer-is-reportedly-in-the-works/
- ScreenRant: https://screenrant.com/half-life-3-reveal-imminent-logic-november-2025/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Valve Software uploads an official teaser trailer for Half-Life 3 (or a differently titled game continuing the Half-Life series) to its verified YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@ValveSoftware) between 2025-11-10 and 2025-11-20 (inclusive). The video must be publicly viewable, at least 30 seconds long, and explicitly labeled or described as a teaser or announcement for a new Half-Life game. Trailers posted after the end date, or on unofficial channels (e.g., third-party leaks, fan accounts), do not count. If the video is later removed but was publicly available during the resolution window, it still counts. Resolution will be determined by direct verification of the YouTube channel. In the event that YouTube becomes inaccessible, resolution will be based on archived versions via the Wayback Machine (https://archive.org/web/) or secondary confirmation from Valve’s official Steam news feed (https://store.steampowered.com/news/?appids=570,730,440,232090).
subquestions.rationale: The release of an official teaser trailer by Valve would be a strong leading indicator that Half-Life 3 is nearing public announcement and likely on track for a 2025 release. Given that insider reports suggest the trailer is already in production and that Valve typically announces and releases games in close succession (e.g., Half-Life: Alyx), a teaser within this narrow window would significantly increase the probability of the ultimate question resolving 'Yes'. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but instead tracks a distinct, observable milestone that would signal active, public movement toward release.

question: Will Trump publicly disparage Netanyahu by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump makes any public statement in which he insults, mocks, or attacks Benjamin Netanyahu personally or professionally in a clearly negative manner by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

This includes calling Netanyahu weak, stupid, disloyal, a failure, using an insulting nickname, or using other derogatory language. Policy disagreements stated without disparaging language will not count.

Any public statement made by Trump qualifies.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a credible news outlet report that a senior advisor or ally of Donald Trump has publicly criticized Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership or policies between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu have been simmering beneath the surface despite public displays of alliance. While Trump has praised Netanyahu in the past, recent actions—such as Trump claiming he 'stopped Netanyahu' from continuing the war in Gaza (TIME, Oct 24, 2025)—suggest a growing narrative of unilateral U.S. control over Israeli decisions, which could strain relations (https://time.com/...). On the other hand, Netanyahu has made statements perceived as mocking or defiant toward U.S. leadership, including during his Qatar-related airstrike controversy, where Haaretz reported that 'Netanyahu made a mockery of Trump in Qatar - and paid no price for it' (https://www.haaretz.com/...). Additionally, policy disagreements over Iran have already surfaced, with Worthy Christian News reporting 'sharp disagreements' during a May 2025 call, where Trump favored diplomacy while Israel emphasized military objectives (https://www.worthynews.com/...). Given Trump’s sensitivity to loyalty and public perception, criticism of Netanyahu by a close Trump ally may signal a shift in tone that precedes a direct public disparagement by Trump himself. Such indirect signals often precede more direct confrontations in political discourse, especially in the Trump orbit where surrogates frequently test messaging before principals escalate. As of October 2025, no direct insult from Trump toward Netanyahu has occurred, but the rhetorical space is heating up.

Sources:
- TIME: https://time.com/7284988/trump-netanyahu-gaza-ceasefire/
- Haaretz: https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2025-09-16/ty-article/.premium/netanyahu-made-a-mockery-of-trump-in-qatar-and-paid-no-price-for-it/00000192-1f8f-d3f6-a5d3-5fbf9d9a0000
- Worthy Christian News: https://www.worthynews.com/trump-netanyahu-call-reportedly-marked-by-sharp-disagreements-over-iran-strategy
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), a credible news outlet reports that a senior advisor or public ally of Donald Trump has made a public statement criticizing Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership or policies in clearly negative terms—such as calling him weak, ineffective, disloyal, or a failure, or using similarly derogatory language. A 'senior advisor or public ally' includes individuals who have held senior roles in Trump’s administration (e.g., former cabinet members, senior White House staff) or who are frequently cited as Trump confidants (e.g., Rudy Giuliani, Kellyanne Conway, Jason Miller, Charlie Kirk, or JD Vance), or who have been designated as campaign spokespersons or senior advisors as of 2025.

Public statements include remarks made on television, radio, social media (e.g., X/Twitter, Truth Social), podcasts, or in published op-eds. The criticism must go beyond policy disagreement and include personal or professional disparagement.

Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from at least two major English-language news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, The Washington Post, CNN, Reuters, AP, BBC, Politico, Axios, or TIME) published before 2025-11-25. If no such reports exist, or if reports are retracted or discredited, the question resolves No.

If the primary sources become unavailable, secondary verification via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/) or official transcripts from C-SPAN (https://www.c-span.org/) may be used. Events postponed beyond the resolution window do not count. Speculative or anonymous sourcing (e.g., 'a source close to Trump') does not qualify unless corroborated by a named individual’s public statement.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of deteriorating relations between Trump and Netanyahu. Given Trump’s tendency to respond to messaging tested by allies, public criticism of Netanyahu by a senior Trump associate would suggest growing friction within Trump’s orbit, increasing the likelihood that Trump himself may escalate to direct disparagement. It avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on a proxy signal—statements by allies—that is both observable and informative. Because such statements often precede direct attacks in political discourse, resolution of this question could significantly update forecasters’ beliefs about the probability of Trump personally disparaging Netanyahu by January 2026.

question: Will Russia enter Toretske by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Toretske by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Toretske is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces be assessed to have advanced within 10 kilometers of Toretske, according to ISW or DeepStateMap, between November 28, 2025, and December 28, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Toretske is a strategically located settlement in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine, situated west of Bakhmut and near key supply routes. As of late November 2025, Russian forces have been making incremental advances in the eastern and northeastern sectors of Ukraine, particularly around Pokrovsk and Kupiansk. According to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), Russian advances have been characterized by slow, foot-pace gains, often using infiltration tactics and drone warfare. While Toretske itself has not yet been directly engaged, Russian advances in nearby areas—such as the reported entry into the Prigorodny area of Pokrovsk—suggest a broader push toward consolidating control in central Donetsk Oblast. Capturing Toretske would represent a significant step toward encircling Ukrainian forces in the region and advancing toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk, the last major Ukrainian-held cities in Donetsk. As of November 28, 2025, no open-source maps indicate Russian presence within 10 kilometers of Toretske’s administrative boundary. However, continued pressure in adjacent areas increases the likelihood of probing operations toward Toretske in the coming weeks.

Sources:
- ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment (August 31, 2025): https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-31-2025
- DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/
- The Straits Times, 'Russia says its forces advance in embattled Ukrainian city of Pokrovsk' (November 3, 2025): https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/russia-says-its-forces-advance-in-embattled-ukrainian-city-of-pokrovsk
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28, either the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Ukraine map or DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) assesses that Russian forces have advanced to a point within 10 kilometers of the administrative boundary of Toretske, as measured by the closest point on the ISW or DeepStateMap front-line indicator. The assessment must persist through at least one full daily update cycle (i.e., appear on two consecutive daily maps or reports, or be confirmed in a subsequent update if a day is skipped). Temporary glitches, map errors, or one-off annotations not sustained in subsequent updates do not count.

The primary source is the ISW Ukraine map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375. If ISW ceases publication, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) will be used as the secondary source. If both sources become permanently unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of reporting from at least two credible open-source intelligence (OSINT) platforms or major international news outlets (e.g., BBC, Reuters, The Guardian, or Associated Press) confirming the advance.

An advance is defined as the presence of Russian military units or control assessed by the source within the 10 km radius, including areas shaded under 'Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine', 'Assessed Russian Control', 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine', or 'Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours'. A negotiated or de jure transfer of control does not count unless accompanied by physical presence within the zone. If Russian forces enter the area but withdraw before the end date, the question still resolves Yes if the condition was met during the resolution window.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of Russian momentum toward Toretske. While the ultimate question asks whether Russia captures any part of Toretske by January 1, 2026, a 10-kilometer approach would signal a significant escalation in operational reach and intent. Given the current front-line dynamics and the slow pace of Russian advances (approximately 440–500 km per month in recent months, per ISW), closing within 10 km of Toretske by late December would imply a high probability of eventual entry into the settlement. This subquestion avoids being a mere restatement of the ultimate question by focusing on proximity rather than control, providing forecasters with a measurable, high-value signal of battlefield momentum. It is also unlikely to resolve to Yes or No with near-certainty, preserving informational value.

question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The difference will be calculated as the December 2024 value minus the December 2025 value.

The December 2024 figure will be based on the initial December 2024 BLS Employment Situation report scheduled for release on January 3, 2025, and the initial December 2025 figure will be based on the report scheduled for release on January 9, 2026. Revisions made to these figures will not be considered, only the values reported in the initial reports will be used.

The resolution source will be the BLS Employment Situation data, specifically the series CES9091000001, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 or the official BLS website.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) report a net decrease in seasonally adjusted federal government employment between November 30, 2025, and December 30, 2025, based on the initial December 2025 Employment Situation report?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question hinges on whether Elon Musk and DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency) will succeed in cutting 100,000–150,000 federal employees in 2025, as measured by the BLS 'All Employees, Federal' series (CES9091000001). As of the most recent available data, federal employment stood at approximately 2.8 million, according to the BLS. The BLS typically releases monthly employment data with a one-month lag, meaning the December 2025 report will be published in January 2026. However, early signals about federal employment trends may be inferred from the timing and content of the December report's release and any preliminary announcements or leaks. Recent news indicates that the BLS has faced operational disruptions, including a federal government shutdown that delayed data collection and reporting (e.g., no BLS reports issued after August 2025 until December 2025). The November 2025 jobs report was rescheduled to December 16, 2025, due to incomplete data collection, suggesting that the BLS may face challenges in producing timely and accurate reports. A net decrease in federal employment during the final month of 2025 would be an early signal that large-scale layoffs are underway, especially if the drop exceeds typical seasonal fluctuations. Conversely, stable or increasing federal employment would suggest that the 100k–150k reduction target is unlikely to be met. The BLS Employment Situation report is the authoritative source for this data and will be used to resolve both the subquestion and the ultimate question.

Sources:
- BLS Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm
- FRED Series CES9091000001: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001
- TalkMarkets on BLS delays (Nov 2025): https://www.talkmarkets.com/content/economic-insight/bls-nonfarm-jobs-revisions-are-negative-26-out-of-last-32-months?page=2
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports, in the initial December 2025 Employment Situation report (scheduled for release on January 9, 2026), that the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees (as measured by series CES9091000001) decreased between the November 2025 value and the December 2025 value, with the change occurring within the period from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30. The resolution will be based solely on the initial release of the December 2025 data, not on any subsequent revisions. The data must come from the official BLS Employment Situation report, available at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm or the FRED database at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001. If the report is not published by January 15, 2026, or if the federal employment data is missing or marked as unreliable (e.g., flagged due to incomplete collection), the question resolves as 'No'. A decrease of one or more employees is sufficient for a 'Yes' resolution.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a direct early indicator of whether large-scale federal employment reductions are occurring in the final month of 2025. Given that the ultimate question depends on a cumulative drop of 100,000–150,000 federal jobs over the entire year, a net decrease in the last month—especially one larger than normal seasonal variation—would increase the likelihood that the target is being pursued and partially achieved. Conversely, no decrease or an increase would suggest that the Musk/DOGE downsizing initiative is not materializing or is being delayed. Because the BLS report is the definitive source for the ultimate question, this subquestion leverages the same data stream but focuses on a narrow, time-limited window to provide timely signal value. It avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on month-to-month momentum at a critical juncture.

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pakistan initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Indian territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Pakistani military forces that impact Indian territory (e.g., if a Pakistani missile or drone hits a target within India’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Indian territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Indian soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Pakistani ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Pakistan conduct a test of a new or upgraded ballistic missile with a range capable of reaching major Indian cities (≥250 km) between October 15, 2025, and November 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pakistan's missile development program has long been a key indicator of its strategic posture toward India. The Fatah-II missile, with a range of up to 400 km, has already been used in past strikes during the May 2025 escalation, targeting locations such as Sirsa in Haryana (indiatoday.in, 2025-05-10). Pakistan has also demonstrated capabilities with cruise and ballistic missiles during 'Operation Bunyan Ul Marsoos,' signaling its willingness to employ long-range precision weapons against Indian military and civilian infrastructure. Recent hostilities revealed that Pakistan is actively deploying advanced missile systems, including guided rockets like the Fatah-1 (140 km range) and longer-range systems capable of striking deep into Indian territory. A successful test of a new or upgraded missile with a range exceeding 250 km—a threshold that includes most of northern and western India—would indicate ongoing investment in strike capabilities and could signal renewed intent or preparedness for future military action. Such tests are typically conducted at known ranges like the Sonmiani test facility and are often followed by official announcements or satellite imagery confirmation. Given the fragile ceasefire following the May 2025 conflict, any new missile test would be closely watched as a potential precursor to renewed hostilities.

Sources:
- India Today – Fatah-1 debris found in Srinagar: https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pak-fatah-1-rocket-debris-dal-lake-srinagar-jammu-kashmir-2717238-2025-09-22
- India Today – Fateh-II missile used in strikes: https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pakistan-operation-bunyan-ul-marsoos-missile-strikes-india-pahalgam-attack-2714586-2025-05-10
- NDTV – Pakistan's retaliation with missiles and drones: https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/pakistan-retaliation-operation-bunyan-ul-marsoos-drone-missile-attacks-india-2714586
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Pakistan conducts a test of a ballistic missile (including guided surface-to-surface missiles) with a range of at least 250 kilometers between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 (inclusive), as confirmed by credible public reporting from at least two independent, reliable sources. A 'test' is defined as a deliberate launch of a missile by Pakistani military or defense research agencies (e.g., Strategic Plans Division or NESCOM) for the purpose of evaluating performance, range, accuracy, or new capabilities. The missile must be newly developed or a significantly upgraded variant (e.g., extended range, new guidance system, or improved payload) compared to previously tested models. Evidence may include official statements from Pakistani authorities, satellite imagery (e.g., from Planet Labs or Maxar), or reports from defense monitoring organizations such as the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), Missile Threat Project at CSIS, or Jane’s. 

Resolution sources:
- CSIS Missile Threat Project: https://missilethreat.csis.org/country/pakistan/
- IISS Military Balance reports: https://www.iiss.org/publications/military-balance
- Jane’s Defence Weekly: https://www.janes.com/defence-news
- Planet Labs satellite imagery (publicly accessible): https://www.planet.com/

If no such test is confirmed by these sources during the specified period, the question resolves No. If the test is announced but later retracted, or if sources conflict and no consensus emerges, the question resolves to Ambiguous. If a missile is launched but not confirmed as a test (e.g., accidental launch or operational strike), it does not count. Tests of missiles with ranges under 250 km (e.g., Fatah-I) do not qualify. If the only evidence comes from unverified social media or single-source intelligence without corroboration, the question may resolve to Ambiguous.
subquestions.rationale: A missile test by Pakistan involving a system capable of reaching major Indian cities is a strong indicator of military posturing and readiness, which could precede or escalate toward direct strikes. Following the May 2025 conflict, Pakistan's restraint in not conducting such tests may have signaled de-escalation. A resumption of testing—especially of longer-range or upgraded systems—would suggest renewed offensive capability development and could reflect intent to maintain pressure on India. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but provides early evidence of Pakistan's strategic trajectory. It is informative because such tests are observable, verifiable, and closely tied to military doctrine and escalation dynamics. A positive outcome would increase the probability of future aerial strikes, while the absence of such tests would suggest continued restraint.

The deployment of this system could indicate a shift toward more proactive and localized drone interdiction, reducing reliance on fighter jets for interception. Current capabilities include kinetic systems (e.g., missiles) and non-kinetic methods like jammers, with the new system likely falling into the latter category to enable safer operations over populated areas.

As of September 26, 2025, there has been no formal indictment, but internal pressure from senior DOJ leadership is mounting. subquestions.question: Will SpaceX publicly announce the completion of stacking Starship Vehicle 30 (Ship 30) and Booster 14 at Starbase, Texas, between October 18, 2025, and November 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Starship Flight Test 12 is expected to use the next fully integrated vehicle stack after Ship 29 and Booster 13, likely designated Ship 30 and Booster 14. As of October 14, 2025, SpaceX successfully completed Flight Test 11 using Ship 29 and Booster 13. Post-flight, SpaceX typically begins stacking the next vehicle while analyzing data from the prior test. Stacking—the process of mating the upper stage (Ship) and the first stage (Booster) on the orbital launch mount—is a necessary precursor to any launch campaign and includes integration with the launch tower, ground systems, and propellant loading tests. According to NASASpaceFlight.com, stacking timelines have varied between 2–6 weeks depending on hardware readiness and facility upgrades. As of mid-2025, SpaceX has been averaging one Starship test flight every 3–4 weeks when no major failures occur, but stacking must be completed before a launch can be scheduled. Public confirmation of stacking completion typically comes via SpaceX’s X (formerly Twitter) account, official webcast commentary, or imagery from reliable observers such as the NSF Starbase team or Everyday Astronaut’s live stream.

Sources:
- NASASpaceFlight.com - Starship development updates: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/tag/starship/
- SpaceX X account: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
- NSF Starbase live feed: https://nsfstarbase.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if SpaceX publicly announces or if credible, verifiable public evidence (such as official SpaceX social media posts, live webcast statements, or high-confidence imagery from established spaceflight observers like NASASpaceFlight.com or Everyday Astronaut) confirms that Starship Ship 30 and Booster 14 have been fully stacked on the orbital launch mount at Starbase, Texas, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive).

Public announcements include:
- A post on SpaceX’s official X account (@SpaceX) stating or showing the stacking completion.
- Commentary during an official SpaceX webcast confirming the stack.
- A report from NASASpaceFlight.com or similar authoritative spaceflight publication with photographic or telemetry evidence of the fully stacked vehicle on the pad.

Imagery must clearly show both Ship 30 and Booster 14 mated and vertical on the orbital launch mount. Stacking must be complete; partial integration (e.g., booster on pad without ship) does not count.

If no such announcement or evidence emerges by 2025-11-17, the question resolves No.

Fall-back sources: In the event the primary sources are unavailable, resolution will use archived content from https://web.archive.org or reports from SpaceNews (https://spacenews.com) or Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/science/) with equivalent evidentiary standards.

If the stacking is completed but no verifiable public evidence is released by 2025-11-17, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Stacking of the next Starship vehicle is a necessary milestone before any launch campaign can proceed. Flight Test 12 cannot occur unless Ship 30 and Booster 14 (or their designated equivalents) are fully stacked and integrated at Starbase. Given that Flight Test 11 occurred on October 13, 2025, stacking of the next vehicle would typically begin within days and be completed within 2–4 weeks under normal operations. Therefore, observing stacking by November 17 is a strong leading indicator that Flight Test 12 is on track for a November 30 launch. Conversely, failure to stack by mid-November would suggest delays that make a late-November launch unlikely, making this a high-value informational crux for forecasting the ultimate question.

subquestions.question: Will South Korean prosecutors file a formal sentencing recommendation for Han Duck-soo in his martial law trial between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25?

The trial is ongoing, and a key procedural step before sentencing is the prosecution's formal sentencing recommendation, which typically occurs after closing arguments and before the court delivers its verdict. In South Korean criminal procedure, the prosecution presents a final argument that includes a specific sentencing demand (e.g., years in prison), which is a strong signal of the likely outcome of the trial. The timing of this recommendation can indicate judicial progress and prosecutorial confidence in securing a conviction. Given that Han’s trial is active and high-profile, the filing of a sentencing recommendation would be a significant milestone toward a potential prison sentence before 2027.

question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
