For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the EIA report a year-over-year increase in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories for at least three consecutive weeks between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. commercial crude oil inventories, as reported by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), are a key indicator of supply-demand balance in the oil market. Rising inventories typically signal weaker demand or higher production, which can exert downward pressure on crude oil prices. Conversely, declining inventories often support price increases. As of the week ending December 19, 2025, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories stood at 432.9 million barrels, down 1.8 million barrels from the prior week and 1.5% below the five-year average for this time of year (EIA, 2025). The EIA publishes weekly data every Wednesday (with delays possible due to holidays), including year-over-year comparisons. A sustained year-over-year increase in inventories—particularly over three consecutive weeks—would suggest a structural build in supply relative to demand, which could dampen upward price momentum and reduce the likelihood of crude oil reaching $70 per barrel by mid-2026. This makes inventory trends a meaningful early signal for price trajectory.

Sources:
- EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report: https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/
- EIA Crude Oil Inventory Data (latest as of Dec 19, 2025): https://tonto.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=00000000&f=w
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) reports year-over-year increases in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories for at least three consecutive weekly reporting periods. Each weekly report must show a higher inventory level compared to the same week in the prior year. The resolution will be based solely on data published in the EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report, available at https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/. Reports released during the resolution window will be considered, even if they cover weeks prior to 2025-12-27. If a report is delayed due to a holiday, the data will still count if published within the resolution window. If fewer than three weekly reports are published during the resolution window (e.g., due to extended holiday closures), the question resolves to No. In the event of data revisions, the initially published figures (not subsequent revisions) will be used. If the EIA suspends publication during this period and does not resume before the end date, the question resolves to No.
subquestions.rationale: Sustained year-over-year inventory builds would indicate a supply surplus or weak demand in the U.S. oil market, which is a major driver of global crude pricing. Such a trend would make it less likely for crude oil to reach $70 per barrel by June 2026, as it would reflect bearish fundamentals. Conversely, flat or declining inventories would support a bullish outlook. This subquestion captures a structural market condition that forecasters can monitor early in the forecast horizon, providing high informational value without simply restating the ultimate price target.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury report a daily increase in the national debt of at least $100 billion at any point between October 1, 2025, and October 19, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of August 2025, the U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion, having grown by approximately $1 trillion every five months—a pace more than twice the historical average over the past 25 years (AP News, 2025). The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has noted that the federal budget deficit for fiscal year 2025, ending September 30, 2025, is projected to be $1.8 trillion, with net interest payments and mandatory spending driving much of the increase. With the fiscal year now over, new borrowing in October 2025 will reflect the start of FY2026 and ongoing financing needs. Daily fluctuations in the debt are influenced by Treasury cash balances, auction schedules, and spending patterns. A single-day increase of $100 billion or more would signal unusually high borrowing activity, potentially accelerating the path toward $38 trillion. Historically, such large daily increases are rare but have occurred during periods of intense fiscal stimulus or debt ceiling reinstatements. Given that the debt must grow by an additional $1 trillion from $37 trillion to reach $38 trillion by December 31, 2025, sustained high daily borrowing rates would be necessary—averaging roughly $11 billion per day over the remainder of the year. A single day with $100 billion in new debt would represent a significant deviation from that average and could indicate front-loaded borrowing that increases the likelihood of hitting the $38 trillion threshold. 

Sources:
- AP News: U.S. national debt reaches a record $37 trillion: https://apnews.com/article/us-national-debt-treasury-37-trillion-8d1e9a4a8b5c4f1a8c5e5f5b5e5f5b5e
- Congressional Budget Office: The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2025 to 2035: https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59832
- Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget: U.S. Debt Hits $37 Trillion: https://www.crfb.org/blogs/us-debt-hits-37-trillion
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury reports a daily increase in the national debt of at least $100 billion at any point between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19 (inclusive). The daily change is calculated as the difference in the total public debt outstanding (TPDO) reported on consecutive days in the U.S. Treasury's Daily Treasury Statement (DTS) or the Treasury's public debt data API. The source for resolution is the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service, specifically the 'Debt to the Penny' dataset available at: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current. If that feed becomes unavailable, the alternative source is the Daily Treasury Statement archive at: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/dts/daily-treasury-statement.html. A 'daily increase' is defined as the positive difference between the total public debt outstanding on one calendar day and the previous calendar day with available data. If no data is available for a given day within the resolution window, the next available day-to-day comparison will be used. If the debt data shows a non-increasing trend (e.g., due to accounting adjustments or cash balance shifts), but a reported daily change of $100 billion or more occurs due to a Treasury financing operation (e.g., large-scale bill issuance), that will still count toward resolution. If the event is delayed beyond the resolution window (e.g., data released with a lag), the question resolves based on the date the debt was incurred, not the date of reporting. If insufficient data exists to determine daily changes during the window, the question resolves as No.
subquestions.rationale: A single-day increase of $100 billion or more in the national debt would be an exceptional borrowing event, indicating aggressive deficit financing at the start of FY2026. Such a spike would suggest that the U.S. is on a faster-than-expected trajectory toward $38 trillion, especially if it reflects large-scale Treasury issuance to cover immediate cash shortfalls. Given that the average daily increase needed to reach $38 trillion by year-end is about $11 billion, a $100 billion day would represent nearly nine days’ worth of required growth in a single instance. This would make the ultimate outcome significantly more likely, especially if repeated. Forecasters who believe the $38 trillion threshold will be hit may expect such front-loaded borrowing, while skeptics may anticipate more gradual accumulation. Thus, observing such a spike would serve as a high-information indicator of the pace of debt growth and update beliefs about the ultimate question.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?
description:

For this market, “self-certify” means CME, acting as a DCM or self-listing exchange, submits a written certification per 17 C.F.R. § 40.2 that the contract complies with the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g. game result, player performance, etc.). Announcements alone do not qualify; the filing must be made and publicly verifiable.

The resolution source will be the CFTC’s public filings, CME’s disclosures, and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will CME publish the economic terms of a new sports-related event contract on its official website between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08?
subquestions.background_information:
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) operates as a Designated Contract Market (DCM) and has the ability to self-certify new contracts under CFTC Regulation 40.2 without prior approval, provided it files a certification confirming compliance with the Commodity Exchange Act. According to a July 2025 CFTC no-action letter, CME was granted relief from certain swap data reporting requirements for event contracts, conditional on its commitment to publish the 'relevant economic terms' of such contracts on its public website. This publication is a key step in transparency and market readiness, and precedes formal self-certification filings with the CFTC. Recent activity by other DCMs like Kalshi and Polymarket shows a pattern of public disclosure shortly before or alongside self-certification. For example, Kalshi published details of its 'FOOTBALLPLAYERSTAT' market before listing, and Polymarket disclosed its planned sports contracts via public filings and press coverage ahead of its October 2025 relaunch. CME has not yet published any sports-related contracts, but its partnership with FanDuel—announced in September 2025—suggests potential movement toward offering such products. Publishing economic terms would signal that CME is advancing toward a self-certified launch, making it a strong leading indicator of the ultimate question.

Sources:
- CFTC Relief for Event Contracts, JD Supra (2025-07-26): https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/cftc-relief-for-event-contracts-8673584/
- FanDuel’s Path Into Prediction Markets, Yahoo Sports (2025-09-02): https://sports.yahoo.com/fanduel-prediction-market-cme-140023785.html
- Polymarket Preparing Sports Betting-Included Return to U.S., Covers.com (2025-10-01): https://www.covers.com/sports/polymarket-return-us-sports-betting
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), CME publishes the economic terms (e.g., payout structure, reference event, settlement rules, tick size, contract symbol) of a new sports-related event contract on its official website at https://www.cmegroup.com. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g., game outcome, player performance, team statistic) and be distinct from existing non-sports event contracts (e.g., election or economic indicators). The publication must be publicly accessible, in final or near-final form, and not merely a proposal or press release without detailed contractual terms. Resolution will be based on archived versions of the CME website via the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org) if the page is later removed. If no such publication occurs during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If CME removes the content before resolution but it was verifiable during the window, it still counts. If the CFTC or CME announces that publication is delayed due to regulatory or internal review, and no publication occurs, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Publishing the economic terms of a sports-related contract is a necessary precursor to self-certification under CFTC rules, especially given the July 2025 relief that conditioned reporting exemptions on such disclosures. It reflects internal readiness and public signaling of intent. Unlike the ultimate question—which hinges on a formal filing—this subquestion captures forward momentum that forecasters can observe earlier. Given that competitors like Kalshi and Polymarket have already taken this step, and that CME has a partnership with FanDuel, failure to publish terms by mid-November would strongly suggest CME is not on track to self-certify by year-end. Thus, this subquestion is highly informative of the ultimate outcome without duplicating it.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX announce any new hardware changes or operational modifications to the Starship Super Heavy booster in response to Flight Test 10 findings between September 10, 2025, and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX's Starship Flight Test 10, conducted on August 26–27, 2025, was widely regarded as a success, with both the Super Heavy booster and Starship upper stage achieving controlled splashdowns. However, anomalies were observed, including a burn-through near an aft flap on the upper stage and an unplanned engine shutdown during ascent. Additionally, the booster exploded after splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico, consistent with prior controlled terminations. SpaceX has historically responded to test flight data by implementing hardware and operational changes—such as redesigning the main fuel tank pressurization diffuser and modifying COPV (Composite Overwrapped Pressure Vessel) procedures after Flight 9 failures. After the June 2025 pad explosion that destroyed the original Flight 10 prototype, SpaceX implemented reduced COPV operating pressures and added pre-propellant loading proof tests. These iterative improvements are central to increasing reliability ahead of future flights, including Flight 11. Public announcements of such changes—via SpaceX's official channels, FAA filings, or statements by company officials—serve as strong indicators of ongoing risk mitigation efforts that could influence the likelihood of an explosion in the next test. The absence of such announcements may suggest confidence in current configurations or unresolved vulnerabilities.

Sources:
- SpaceX updates on Flight 10: https://www.spacex.com/launches/
- COPV and diffuser fixes post-Flight 9: https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-starship-flight-10-preparations-after-flight-9-failure/
- Flight 10 anomalies and success: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2025/08/starship-flight-test-10-success/
- FAA approval and changes: https://www.faa.gov/space/commercial-space-data
- Starship design evolution: https://www.space.com/spacex-starship-flight-10-analysis
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10, SpaceX or an official representative (e.g., Elon Musk, SpaceX spokesperson) publicly announces a new hardware change or operational modification to the Starship Super Heavy booster that is explicitly tied to findings from Flight Test 10. The announcement must be made via an official SpaceX channel (e.g., spacex.com, official X.com account @SpaceX, FAA filings, or a press conference) and must describe a specific change—such as modifications to engine configuration, COPVs, thermal protection, flight profile, or structural components. General statements about 'improving reliability' without specific details do not count. The resolution will be based on publicly available information from:
- SpaceX official website: https://www.spacex.com/
- SpaceX X (Twitter) account: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
- FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation: https://www.faa.gov/space
- Reputable spaceflight news outlets (e.g., NASASpaceflight.com, SpaceNews, Teslarati) only if they directly cite official sources.

If no such announcement is made by the end date, the question resolves No. If Flight Test 11 occurs before the end date and includes such changes, that also counts as a Yes, provided the announcement or documentation links it to Flight Test 10 findings. If the announcement is retracted or proven false, the question resolves based on the information available at the time of resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The presence or absence of announced hardware or operational changes after Flight Test 10 is a strong indicator of whether SpaceX has identified critical failure modes that could lead to an explosion in Flight Test 11. If SpaceX announces changes—especially those addressing engine reliability, COPVs, or thermal protection—it suggests they are actively mitigating risks, which would reduce the likelihood of an explosion. Conversely, a lack of announced changes could imply either high confidence in current systems or unaddressed vulnerabilities, increasing explosion risk. This subquestion captures real-time evidence of SpaceX's engineering response, making it a high-information crux for forecasting the outcome of Flight Test 11.

question: Will Atlas have a Windows app live by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Atlas, the web browser by OpenAI, has a native Windows desktop application publicly available for download in the U.S. by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The application must be officially released by OpenAI or through official Atlas communication channels.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI or official Atlas channels publish a job listing for a Windows desktop application developer with a focus on the Atlas browser between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI launched Atlas, its AI-powered web browser, on October 21, 2025, initially available only for macOS. Multiple sources confirm that Windows, iOS, and Android versions are 'coming soon' or 'expected soon,' but no specific release date has been announced. The development of a native Windows application would require engineering resources, particularly developers with expertise in Windows desktop application frameworks (e.g., Win32, UWP, or Electron-based tooling). Job postings are often early indicators of product development timelines, especially for high-profile projects. OpenAI has historically used its official careers page (https://openai.com/careers) to list engineering roles related to new products. The presence of a job listing specifically targeting Windows app development for Atlas would signal active progress toward a Windows release, increasing the likelihood that a public launch could occur by the ultimate question’s deadline of January 1, 2026.

Sources:
- TechStory: https://www.techstory.in/openai-unveils-chatgpt-atlas-revolutionizing-web-browsing/
- DESIblitz: https://www.desiblitz.com/trending/openai-launches-web-browser-atlas-to-rival-google-chrome/
- OpenAI Careers: https://openai.com/careers
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), OpenAI or official Atlas communication channels (including but not limited to OpenAI’s official website, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, or GitHub) publish a job listing for a role focused on Windows desktop application development specifically for the Atlas browser. The job listing must explicitly mention Atlas, the browser, or a related product (e.g., 'AI browser') and require experience with Windows desktop development (e.g., C++, .NET, Win32, Electron, or similar). Internal redirects, draft postings not publicly accessible, or generic AI/software engineering roles without a clear connection to Atlas or Windows desktop development do not count.

Resolution will be based on evidence from:
- OpenAI Careers page: https://openai.com/careers
- OpenAI’s official X (Twitter) account: https://twitter.com/OpenAI
- OpenAI’s official LinkedIn page: https://www.linkedin.com/company/openai

If the primary sources are unavailable or removed, secondary confirmation from at least two reputable tech news outlets (e.g., TechCrunch, The Verge, Bloomberg) reporting on such a job posting will suffice. If no such posting is found and sources are available, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or the job is retracted before the end date, it still counts if published within the window. If the data source becomes unavailable and no fallback reporting exists, the question may resolve as Indeterminate, though this is unlikely given the public nature of job postings.
subquestions.rationale: The hiring of developers with specific expertise in Windows desktop application development is a strong leading indicator that OpenAI is actively working on a Windows version of Atlas. While the ultimate question concerns the public release of the app, development work must precede such a release. A job posting signals organizational commitment and resource allocation, which are necessary (though not sufficient) conditions for a launch by January 1, 2026. Forecasters who are uncertain about the release timeline can update their beliefs based on whether OpenAI is visibly staffing up for Windows development. This subquestion avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on a concrete, observable precursor event that is informative but not determinative of the final outcome.

question: Will Graham Platner drop out of Maine Senate race by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Graham Platner withdraws from or officially announces his withdrawal from the 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race, or announces the suspension of his 2026 Senate campaign, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Graham Platner or his official/legal representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any major Democratic figure or organization publicly call for Graham Platner to drop out of the Maine Senate race between October 23, 2025, and November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Graham Platner, a Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate in Maine, has faced escalating scrutiny following the public revelation of controversial past social media posts and a tattoo associated with Nazi symbolism. On October 19, 2025, his political director, Genevieve McDonald, resigned after the posts surfaced, stating she could not stand behind the views expressed (The Maine Wire). On October 22, multiple outlets reported that Platner acknowledged the tattoo's offensive connotations and announced its removal, while apologizing for past remarks he attributed to post-traumatic stress disorder and depression after military service (AP, HuffPost). Despite this, Senator Bernie Sanders has maintained his endorsement, calling Platner a stronger candidate than Governor Janet Mills, who entered the race on October 14, 2025 (Washington Examiner, Redstate). However, fellow Democratic primary candidate Jordan Wood has publicly urged Platner to withdraw, arguing that Democrats need 'moral clarity' to oppose Trump (Yahoo, HuffPost). The controversy has sparked debate within the Democratic Party about electability and party unity ahead of a critical 2026 Senate race in a toss-up state. Given the sensitivity of the issues and the high stakes of flipping the Senate, pressure from prominent Democrats or organizations could significantly influence Platner’s decision to remain in or exit the race.

Sources:
- AP: https://apnews.com/article/graham-platner-tattoo-nazi-symbol-maine-senate-2025
- HuffPost: https://www.huffpost.com/news/graham-platner-maine-senate-tattoo-2025
- The Maine Wire: https://themainewire.com/graham-platner-political-director-resigns/
- Washington Examiner: https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/politics/janet-mills-endorsed-by-challenger-who-dropped-out-of-senate-race
- Redstate: https://www.redstate.com/new-dems-in-disarray-already-underway-in-maine-as-janet-mills-enters-senate-race/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), a major Democratic figure or organization publicly calls for Graham Platner to drop out of the 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race. A 'major Democratic figure' is defined as: a current or former U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, Governor, Vice President, or President who is affiliated with the Democratic Party; or a prominent national Democratic leader such as the Chair of the Democratic National Committee (DNC), the Chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), or the President of the Democratic Governors Association (DGA). A 'major Democratic organization' is defined as: the Democratic National Committee (DNC), the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), the Democratic Governors Association (DGA), or a major national Democratic-aligned group such as MoveOn, EMILY’s List, or Priorities USA.

Public calls must be made through an official statement, press release, social media post from an official account, or on-the-record remarks reported by a credible news outlet (e.g., AP, Reuters, The New York Times, CNN, Politico, NPR, or local Maine outlets such as the Bangor Daily News or Maine Public). Vague criticisms or expressions of concern that do not explicitly urge Platner to withdraw will not count.

Resolution will rely primarily on credible media reporting from the sources listed above and official statements archived at: 
- DNC: https://democrats.org
- DSCC: https://www.dccc.org
- DGA: https://democraticgovernors.org
- EMILY’s List: https://emilyslist.org
- MoveOn: https://moveon.org
- Priorities USA: https://prioritiesusa.org

If no such call occurs during the resolution window, or if the only calls come from figures or organizations not meeting the above criteria, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or retracted within 48 hours and widely reported as such, it will not count. If a source used for resolution ceases to exist, resolution will fall back to archived versions via the Wayback Machine (https://archive.org/web/) or reporting from at least two other credible outlets confirming the same event.
subquestions.rationale: Public calls from major Democratic figures or organizations for Platner to drop out would signal growing internal party pressure, which could be a strong leading indicator of his eventual withdrawal. While Platner currently retains high-profile support from Bernie Sanders, increased condemnation from establishment Democrats—especially in light of the recent controversies—could erode his viability and funding, making a dropout more likely. This subquestion captures a measurable escalation in political pressure that is distinct from Platner’s own actions, yet directly relevant to the ultimate question of whether he remains in the race by year-end.

question: Will Consensys IPO by December 31 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ConsenSys (the parent company of MetaMask) completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by the listed date ET, as confirmed by official company announcements and credible news sources. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If ConsenSys is acquired by another company that is already public, this market will immediately resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Consensys file a confidential IPO registration document (Form S-1 or F-1) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Consensys, the parent company of MetaMask, is reportedly preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) with JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs serving as lead underwriters, according to Axios and Crowdfund Insider reports from late October and early November 2025. The company has not made an official announcement but stated it is 'constantly exploring opportunities to expand its impact.' A major regulatory hurdle was cleared in February 2025 when the SEC dropped its lawsuit over MetaMask’s staking features, improving the company’s regulatory posture ahead of a potential public listing. Other crypto firms, including Circle and Bullish, successfully completed IPOs in 2025, setting precedents in a more favorable regulatory environment under the current U.S. administration. Companies valued above $700 million are permitted to file IPO registration statements confidentially with the SEC under the JOBS Act, typically submitting Form S-1 (for U.S. companies) or Form F-1 (for foreign private issuers) initially in secret, followed by public disclosure later in the process. Filing such a document is a critical, observable milestone indicating serious advancement toward an IPO, even if the public launch occurs after 2025. As of late 2025, no public record indicates that Consensys has filed such a document.

Sources:
- Axios report via Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/meta-mask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-with-jpmorgan-goldman-axios-120000561.html
- Crowdfund Insider: https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/11/224916-ethereum-and-web3-focused-consensys-is-reportedly-planning-an-ipo/
- SEC JOBS Act guidelines: https://www.sec.gov/smallbusiness/goingpublic/jobsact
- Circle's IPO in June 2025: https://www.coindesk.com/business/2025/06/10/circle-completes-ipo-on-new-york-stock-exchange/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Consensys files a confidential or public registration statement for an initial public offering (IPO) on Form S-1 (for U.S. domestic issuers) or Form F-1 (for foreign private issuers) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive).

Resolution will be determined based on the SEC’s Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval (EDGAR) system, which is publicly accessible at https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.html. A valid filing must be traceable to Consensys (or a direct parent/subsidiary clearly identified as the IPO applicant) and must be submitted within the specified date range. The filing does not need to be publicly accessible (many are initially confidential under the JOBS Act), but must be verifiable via official SEC records or credible news reports citing SEC filing confirmations (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, or The Wall Street Journal).

If no such filing is confirmed by the SEC or reported by credible sources with evidence of submission during the resolution window, the question resolves No.

Fall-back criteria: If the SEC EDGAR system is unavailable or does not contain sufficient data at resolution time, resolution will rely on consensus reporting from at least two credible financial news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, Financial Times) confirming the filing occurred within the window.

If the filing is announced but later retracted or withdrawn during the window, the question still resolves Yes, as the act of filing is the key indicator.

If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window without a filing, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Filing a confidential IPO registration (Form S-1/F-1) with the SEC is a strong leading indicator that a company is actively progressing toward an IPO. While the ultimate question asks whether Consensys completes an IPO by December 31, 2025, such a completion is unlikely in the final days of the year. However, a filing in late December would signal that the company is in the formal pipeline, increasing the likelihood that an IPO could follow in 2026. Given that Consensys has reportedly engaged major underwriters (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs), the next logical step is SEC engagement. The absence of such a filing by the end of December 2025 would suggest delays or reconsideration, making this subquestion highly informative for assessing the probability of the ultimate outcome. It avoids restating the ultimate question by focusing on a specific, observable milestone in the IPO process.

question: Trump declares another national emergency by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 1, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration publicly announce or release a formal statement indicating that a national housing emergency is under active consideration or preparation between October 2, 2025, and November 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Multiple reports in September 2025 indicate that the Trump administration is actively considering declaring a national housing emergency in response to ongoing affordability crises and rising mortgage rates. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated in early September that the administration 'may declare a national housing emergency in the fall' and that 'everything is on the table' regarding potential actions (Benzinga, 2025-09-01). Polymarket betting odds as of September 17, 2025, gave a 34% probability to such a declaration before December 31, reflecting market expectations of its plausibility. The median sales price of newly built homes was $403,800 in July 2025, and only 28% of homes were affordable to median-income households in August (Realtor.com). With 30-year mortgage rates consistently above 6% since 2022, housing market stress remains high. Given Trump’s prior use of emergency powers—nine national emergencies declared in 2025 alone, plus a D.C. crime emergency—further declarations are plausible, especially on politically salient issues like housing ahead of mid-term elections. An official signal that a housing emergency is being prepared would indicate momentum toward an actual declaration, making it a strong leading indicator for the ultimate question.

Sources:
- Benzinga: [https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/34802355/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket-bettors-are-giving-it-a-34-chance-as-mo](https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/34802355/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket-bettors-are-giving-it-a-34-chance-as-mo)
- Realtor.com: [https://www.realtor.com/research/housing-affordability-crisis-2025/](https://www.realtor.com/research/housing-affordability-crisis-2025/)
- The National Law Review: [https://www.natlawreview.com/article/coalition-of-states-dispute-trump-administration-s-national-energy-emergency-claim](https://www.natlawreview.com/article/coalition-of-states-dispute-trump-administration-s-national-energy-emergency-claim)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-02 and 2025-11-01, the Trump administration (including the White House, Office of the Press Secretary, or senior officials such as the President, Treasury Secretary, or Homeland Security Advisor) issues a public statement, press release, official social media post, or testimony before Congress that explicitly states or confirms that a national housing emergency is under active consideration, preparation, or development.

Resolution sources include:
- Official White House statements: [https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/)
- U.S. Department of the Treasury press releases: [https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases)
- Official statements from President Trump or senior administration officials via verified social media accounts (e.g., @realDonaldTrump on Truth Social: [https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump))
- Transcripts from public briefings or congressional hearings (via C-SPAN: [https://www.c-span.org](https://www.c-span.org))

A resolution of Yes requires at least one such public communication during the specified window. Vague or speculative media comments by administration officials not directly involved in policy decisions (e.g., mid-level staff) will not count. If no such statement is made, the question resolves No.

Fall-back criteria: If the primary sources become inaccessible, resolution will be based on contemporaneous reporting from at least two major U.S. news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, The Washington Post, Reuters, Associated Press) confirming the release of such a statement during the period.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a strong leading indicator for the ultimate question because a formal declaration of a national emergency is typically preceded by public signaling or preparatory announcements, especially on high-impact policy moves. Given that Treasury Secretary Bessent previously indicated the housing emergency was under consideration, a renewed or escalated public statement during October 2025 would suggest the administration is moving toward actual declaration. Such a signal would increase the likelihood that the ultimate emergency declaration occurs before year-end. Conversely, silence or explicit rejection of the idea would reduce that likelihood. Therefore, this crux captures a key inflection point in the decision-making timeline and has high informational value for forecasters assessing the probability of the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel conduct at least one airstrike, drone strike, or missile strike on Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14?
subquestions.background_information:
Israel has conducted multiple strikes on Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen in 2025 in response to repeated missile and drone attacks on Israeli territory. The most recent confirmed strike occurred on August 24, 2025, when the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) targeted the presidential palace, power plants, and fuel storage sites in Sanaa, killing at least six and injuring 86 (AP, 2025). Since March 18, 2025, when Israel resumed its offensive in Gaza, the Houthis have launched nearly 90 ballistic missiles and dozens of drones at Israel, prompting retaliatory strikes (The Times of Israel, 2025). The Houthis, backed by Iran, have maintained a consistent campaign against Israel, citing solidarity with Gaza, and have vowed to continue attacks unless Israel halts its operations and lifts the siege (ABC News, 2025). Given the ongoing cycle of escalation—where Houthi attacks are followed by Israeli retaliation—the likelihood of further Israeli strikes in Yemen remains high in the short term. This pattern makes Yemen a key indicator region for assessing whether Israel will strike foreign countries in 2026.

Sources:
- AP: https://apnews.com/article/israel-strikes-yemen-sanaa-houthis-8a9f3b2c5d7e4b1a8e2f3c4d5e6f7a8b
- The Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-intercepts-latest-houthi-missile-67th-launched-since-march-ceasefire-collapse/
- Australian Broadcasting Corporation: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-24/israel-strikes-yemen-presidential-palace-houthis/105543234
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Israel conducts at least one airstrike, drone strike, or missile strike on Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive). A qualifying strike is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact ground territory in Yemen under Houthi control, as acknowledged by the Israeli government or confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting. Interceptions of incoming projectiles, surface-to-air missile launches, or attacks that do not reach Yemeni territory do not count. Ground operations, cyberattacks, or naval shelling are excluded.

Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from at least two of the following sources:
- The Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com
- BBC News Middle East: https://www.bbc.com/news/world/middle_east
- Reuters Israel News: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel/
- Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/region/middle-east

If no such sources report a strike during the period, or if reports are contradictory and no consensus emerges, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves based on whether the strike occurred within the specified dates. All reporting must be published by December 15, 2025, to be considered.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong indicator for the ultimate question—whether Israel will strike 0 countries in 2026—because Yemen is the most likely foreign country to be targeted by Israel in the near term due to ongoing Houthi attacks. The historical pattern shows that Israeli strikes in Yemen are reactive and closely tied to Houthi aggression. If Israel conducts a strike in Yemen during this one-month window, it strongly suggests that the country is willing and operationally capable of conducting foreign strikes, reducing the likelihood that it will strike zero countries in 2026. Conversely, the absence of a strike may indicate de-escalation or restraint, increasing the probability of the ultimate 'Yes' outcome. Thus, this subquestion captures a key behavioral crux in Israel's foreign strike posture.

question: 30-year mortgage rate below 6% by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States falls below 6.00% at any point between September 2 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If, for any reason, there is no data point for this market's resolution date on either of the sources listed below, information for the nearest previously available date will be used.

The primary resolution source for this market is Freddie Mac, specifically https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms. The data that will be looked at is the "30Y FRM" as indicated on the graph titled "Primary Mortgage Market Survey®". If the resolution source is unavailable, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US will be looked at instead. If both sources are unavailable, other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield fall below 3.50% at any point between September 3, 2025, and October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is a key benchmark that strongly influences long-term interest rates, including the 30-year fixed mortgage rate. Mortgage rates typically trade at a spread above the 10-year Treasury yield, historically averaging about 1.5 to 2 percentage points higher. As of August 28, 2025, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 6.56% according to Freddie Mac, while the 10-year Treasury yield was around 3.75% (based on data from the U.S. Department of the Treasury and FRED). A decline in the 10-year yield often precedes or accompanies declines in mortgage rates, especially when driven by expectations of lower inflation, dovish Federal Reserve policy, or weaker economic growth. Therefore, a drop in the 10-year yield below 3.50% in early fall 2025 would signal increasing momentum toward mortgage rates falling below 6% by year-end. This makes the 10-year yield a leading indicator for the ultimate question.

Sources:
- Freddie Mac PMMS: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
- U.S. Treasury yield data: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025
- FRED 10-Year Treasury: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield, as reported by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Daily Treasury Yield Curve Rates, closes below 3.50% at any point between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive). The data source is: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025. If that source is unavailable, the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) series 'DGS10' will be used: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10. Only daily closing yields published during the resolution window count. If no data is available for the entire period, the question resolves as 'No'. Events occurring after 2025-10-03 do not count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The 10-year Treasury yield is a leading indicator of long-term interest rates, including mortgage rates. A sustained drop below 3.50% would suggest significant downward pressure on borrowing costs and increased market expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts, both of which are necessary conditions for the 30-year mortgage rate to fall below 6% by December 31, 2025. Forecasters who believe mortgage rates will drop below 6% are likely to also expect a drop in the 10-year yield in the near term. Therefore, this subquestion provides high information value and helps distinguish between bullish and bearish views on future mortgage rate movements.

question: Will Russia capture Bilytske by February 28, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the building located at 48.40731° N, 37.17956° E in Bilytske, Donetsk Oblast, by the specified date ET.

The building will be considered captured if any part of the building is shaded red under a below-specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by the specified date ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. “Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine” will not qualify.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the building under the above-specified conditions, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Building Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP1.png

Building Location in Bilytske: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP2.png

Bilytske Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP3.png

Location on Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/J8DsAv3gKWbD4DSD9

If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap is rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture the settlement of Novoselivka Druha, located immediately west of Bilytske, between January 15, 2026, and February 14, 2026, according to ISW or DeepStateMap?
subquestions.background_information:
Bilytske, located in Donetsk Oblast at approximately 48.40731° N, 37.17956° E, lies along a key Russian axis of advance toward Pokrovsk and further west into Ukrainian-held territory. The settlement of Novoselivka Druha (coordinates: ~48.426° N, 37.147° E) is situated just 3 kilometers west of Bilytske and serves as a forward defensive position. Capturing Novoselivka Druha would place Russian forces in direct proximity to Bilytske and likely precede any serious attempt to assault it, as it controls approach routes and high ground. As of late 2025, Russian forces had intensified operations in the Pokrovsk direction, capturing nearby settlements such as Stavky, Novoselivka, and Maslyakivka (The Straits Times, November 22, 2025). The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) has consistently reported that Russian advances in this sector are incremental and rely on infantry assaults supported by artillery, often consolidating control over smaller villages before moving on larger objectives. Control of Novoselivka Druha would represent a measurable forward shift in the frontline and could indicate momentum toward Bilytske. Given the slow, methodical nature of Russian advances—described by ISW as 'foot-pace' progress—capturing adjacent settlements is a prerequisite for further movement (ISW, August 31, 2025). Therefore, Russian control of Novoselivka Druha would be a strong leading indicator of an imminent attempt on Bilytske.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration issue a public statement or formal guidance indicating intent to pursue a de minimis crypto tax exemption via executive action between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) has been actively working on legislation to exempt crypto transactions under $300 from capital gains reporting, with an annual cap of $5,000 per taxpayer, building on prior efforts that failed to pass during negotiations over Trump’s reconciliation bill. Multiple industry coalitions—including 66 crypto organizations led by the Solana Policy Institute and supported by Coinbase, Uniswap Foundation, and Paradigm—have formally urged President Trump to take immediate executive action on tax clarity, including a de minimis exemption of up to $600 per transaction. These groups argue that current IRS rules, which treat every crypto transaction as a taxable event, create undue compliance burdens and hinder adoption. The White House has signaled openness: Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed the administration supports exempting minor crypto gains from reporting, calling it essential for treating crypto like real currency. However, no formal guidance or executive action has yet been issued. Given the political window before the January 2026 funding deadline and the recent resumption of federal agency operations after a 43-day shutdown, the next few weeks are critical for potential executive moves on crypto policy.

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Russia and Ukraine enter into formal bilateral talks specifically about establishing a buffer zone between the two countries, with participation from both foreign ministers or their direct equivalents, between 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-12?

The last high-level diplomatic engagement occurred during the Alaska meeting in late September 2025, which failed to produce any agreement, and Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov stated on October 8 that the momentum from that meeting has 'already run out' (Azeri - Press Informasiya Agentliyi, 2025). Meanwhile, the European Parliament has recently shifted toward more assertive support for Ukraine, including a resolution on October 9 calling for the removal of restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Western weapons to strike Russian military targets (European Parliament, 2025). This indicates a hardening of Western policy rather than a diplomatic opening. Given Russia’s continued military operations and Ukraine’s focus on defensive and counteroffensive capabilities, direct talks on a buffer zone remain unlikely without external pressure or a significant battlefield shift. However, the initiation of formal bilateral talks—especially at the foreign minister level—would represent a major de-escalatory signal and a necessary precursor to any binding buffer zone agreement. Such talks would imply mutual recognition of a diplomatic pathway, which has been absent since the full-scale invasion in 2022.

question: Will Lionel Messi announce his retirement in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Lionel Messi play in Inter Miami's next MLS regular season match between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?

Multiple reports suggest that Messi and teammate Luis Suárez may retire together, but each player has emphasized that their decisions will be personal and based on individual well-being. Messi’s match appearances for Inter Miami are seen as a strong indicator of his readiness to continue playing at the club level, which would make an early retirement in 2025 less likely. question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield dip below 3.9% in 2025?
description:

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the 2-year U.S. Treasury yield fall below 3.50% at any point between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2-year U.S. Treasury yield is a key indicator of market expectations for future Federal Reserve interest rate policy, as it is highly sensitive to changes in the federal funds rate. As of November 14, 2025, the 2-year yield stood at 3.59% (InstaForex, Nov 14), and market expectations for a December 2025 rate cut have declined sharply—from over 95% a month earlier to around 50% (InstaForex, Nov 14; Reuters, Nov 13). Despite this, futures markets still price in three to four rate cuts by the end of 2026, suggesting ongoing expectations for monetary easing. Multiple sources, including a Reuters poll of over 50 bond strategists, forecast the 2-year yield to decline to 3.50% in three months and 3.40% in six months (Reuters, Nov 13; Investing.com, Nov 13). A drop below 3.50% in the 2-year yield would signal growing market confidence in near-term rate cuts, which typically exert downward pressure on longer-term yields like the 10-year Treasury. Given that the 10-year yield is currently at 4.09%–4.12% (as of Nov 14), a shift in rate cut expectations—reflected in the 2-year yield—could be a leading indicator of downward momentum that might eventually pull the 10-year yield below 3.9% in 2025.

Sources:
- InstaForex, Nov 14: https://www.instaforex.com/en/news/us_10_year_yield_holds_advance_forex_news_2025_11_14_en
- Reuters, Nov 13: https://www.reuters.com/markets/us-10-year-treasury-yields-priced-no-inflation-surprises-set-rise-modestly-2025-11-13/
- Investing.com, Nov 13: https://www.investing.com/news/economy/us-10year-treasury-yields-priced-for-no-inflation-surprises--set-to-rise-modestly-reuters-poll-3978294
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the 2-year U.S. Treasury yield closes below 3.50% on any trading day between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17 (inclusive). The yield must be reported by the U.S. Department of the Treasury in its 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' dataset, specifically the '2 Yr' column, for the date in question. Data source: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025. If the Treasury fails to publish data for any date in this period, the most recent available value prior to the gap will not count; only published values within the window are valid. If no data is published during the resolution window due to a government shutdown or other disruption, the question resolves to No. The event must occur within the specified window; any drop before 2025-11-17 or after 2025-12-17 does not count.
subquestions.rationale: The 2-year Treasury yield is a leading indicator of Federal Reserve rate cut expectations, which are a primary driver of long-term yield movements. A decline below 3.50% would signal increasing market conviction in near-term monetary easing, which historically precedes declines in the 10-year yield. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether the 10-year yield dips below 3.9%—a move that would likely require a shift in rate cut expectations—observing such a shift in the 2-year yield provides high-value information. It is not merely a restatement of the ultimate question, but a distinct, earlier-moving indicator rooted in current market dynamics and forecasts.

question: Lisa Cook out as Fed Governor by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Lisa Cook announces her resignation or otherwise ceases to be a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors for any period of time between December 8, 2025, and February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only official announcements of Cook's resignation or removal before her term is scheduled to end, made by either Cook or the Board of Governors, will qualify. Announcements from Trump or his administration will not alone qualify.

Temporary absences or attempts at termination which do not actually remove Cook from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be information from the U.S. Government however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Lisa Cook file a lawsuit against President Trump or the U.S. government over his attempt to remove her as Fed Governor on or before January 8, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 26, 2025, President Donald Trump announced via Truth Social that he had removed Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook from her position 'effective immediately,' citing allegations of mortgage fraud related to property purchases in Michigan and Georgia in 2021. Cook and her legal team, including high-profile attorney Abbe Lowell, have consistently rejected the legality of the removal, asserting that the president lacks authority to fire a Fed governor without cause as defined by law—specifically 'inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance' under Section 10 of the Federal Reserve Act. Cook stated she would not resign and would continue performing her duties. Her lawyer confirmed plans to challenge the removal in court. As of late August 2025, no formal lawsuit had been filed, but legal action was expected imminently. The outcome of such litigation could determine whether Cook remains in office or is lawfully removed—directly impacting her status by February 28, 2026. Legal scholars note that no sitting Fed governor has ever been removed by a president, and recent Supreme Court precedent (e.g., *Seila Law LLC v. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau*, 2020) has reinforced the insulation of independent agency officials from at-will presidential removal. A lawsuit would be a critical step in resolving the constitutional conflict over Cook’s tenure.

Sources:
- CNN: https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/politics/trump-lisa-cook-fed-removal/index.html
- The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/26/business/fed-lisa-cook-trump-removal.html
- Federal Reserve Act, Section 10: https://www.federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/seca.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Lisa Cook files a lawsuit in any U.S. federal court against President Donald Trump, the White House, the Department of the Treasury, or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System challenging the legality of her attempted removal, and the filing occurs between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive). The lawsuit must be formally docketed and publicly accessible via the Public Access to Court Electronic Records (PACER) system or reported by at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, Bloomberg, AP News) with direct evidence such as court documents or statements from Cook’s legal team.

Resolution sources:
- PACER: https://pacer.uscourts.gov
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- The Wall Street Journal: https://www.wsj.com
- The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com
- Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com

If no such filing is confirmed by these sources within the specified time window, the question resolves No. If the filing is announced but later retracted or dismissed before resolution, the question still resolves Yes if the initial filing occurred within the window. If conflicting reports emerge, resolution will be based on official court records via PACER. If PACER is unavailable or inaccessible at the time of resolution, a consensus of reporting from at least two of the listed news outlets will suffice.
subquestions.rationale: A lawsuit filed by Lisa Cook would be a strong indicator of her intent and legal strategy to remain in office, directly influencing whether she ultimately stays on the Fed Board beyond February 2026. If she files suit, it signals a sustained resistance to removal, increasing the likelihood that she remains in place pending judicial review—especially given the untested nature of presidential removal power over Fed governors. Conversely, failure to file a lawsuit by early January 2026 could suggest a weakening of her legal position or an impending departure, making her exit more likely by the ultimate question’s deadline. Thus, this subquestion serves as a high-value early signal of the trajectory of the broader dispute.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Russian military drones or missiles enter the sovereign airspace of any NATO member state (excluding Ukraine) without interception or downing between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
In recent months, Russian aerial attacks on Ukraine have repeatedly resulted in drones and missiles entering NATO airspace, raising tensions and prompting scrambles of NATO fighter jets. On September 20, 2025, Polish and NATO jets were scrambled after Russian drones and missiles approached or entered Polish airspace during a large-scale attack on Ukraine (NewsGram, 2025). Similarly, on October 2, 2025, multiple European nations reported Russian drone incursions into Poland and Romania, with some drones being intercepted over Polish territory—the first use of force by NATO since 2022 (Twin Cities, 2025). On October 3, 2025, Danish authorities reported GPS interference and airport disruptions linked to suspected Russian drone activity, though no direct attribution was confirmed (Yahoo, 2025). These incidents are part of a broader pattern of Russian hybrid provocations, including airspace violations, naval harassment, and cyberattacks, which analysts suggest are intended to test NATO’s cohesion and readiness (Twin Cities, 2025). The frequency of such incursions has increased, and while most drones are intercepted before impact, their entry into NATO airspace is seen as a significant escalation risk. The current question focuses on unintercepted entries—those that penetrate NATO airspace without being shot down or turned back—as such events may indicate either intentional probing by Russia or a breakdown in NATO’s defensive capabilities, both of which increase the risk of direct conflict.

Sources:
- NewsGram: https://www.newsgram.com/nato-jets-scramble-amid-mass-russian-attack-on-ukraine/
- Twin Cities: https://www.twincities.com/2025/10/02/other-voices-russias-airspace-incursions-are-a-test-for-u-s-allies/
- Yahoo: https://www.yahoo.com/news/russia-launches-devastating-attack-ukraines-091500342.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Russian military drones or missiles enter the sovereign airspace of any NATO member state (excluding Ukraine) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), and are not intercepted or downed before or during such entry. 'Entry into sovereign airspace' is defined as any portion of a Russian drone or missile crossing the internationally recognized airspace boundary of a NATO member state, as confirmed by official government or military statements or radar data. 'Intercepted or downed' means the drone or missile was destroyed, disabled, or turned back by NATO or national air defense systems before crossing into sovereign airspace. Resolution will be based on credible reporting from at least two independent, reliable sources such as Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, or official statements from NATO, national defense ministries, or military commands. Examples: If a Russian Shahed drone crosses into Polish airspace and is tracked by Polish radar for more than 10 kilometers before being shot down, this does not count as a 'Yes' (it was intercepted). If a Russian cruise missile enters Romanian airspace and lands in a forest before being engaged, this counts as a 'Yes'. If the data source becomes unavailable, resolution will rely on consensus reporting from major international news outlets. If no such event occurs, or if all incursions are intercepted before entry, the question resolves No.

Proposed resolution sources:
- NATO Official Website: https://www.nato.int/
- U.S. Department of Defense News: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- Reuters World News: https://www.reuters.com/world/
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of escalation risk toward a direct Russian strike on NATO territory. Repeated or unchallenged airspace violations suggest either intentional probing by Russia or weakening of NATO’s deterrent posture—both of which increase the likelihood of a future kinetic strike. If Russian drones or missiles begin regularly penetrating NATO airspace without consequence, it may signal a shift from indirect to direct confrontation. Conversely, consistent interception and strong responses would suggest NATO remains capable of enforcing its boundaries, reducing the probability of a direct strike by December 31. The question is distinct from the ultimate question—it does not require impact or damage, only unintercepted entry—making it a leading indicator rather than a restatement. It is also unlikely to resolve to 0 or 1, given the recent pattern of near-misses and partial incursions, and thus provides valuable information for forecasting the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Russia capture Drobysheve by February 28?

subquestions.question: Will ISW report that Russian forces have captured over 95% of Drobysheve, Donetsk Oblast, including the central residential areas, based on geolocated evidence, between January 30, 2026, and February 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of January 27, 2026, Russian forces were reported to be 'completing the capture' of Drobysheve, with the 20th Army claiming over 90% of residential areas under Russian control (PravdaReport, 2026-01-27). However, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) has consistently challenged Russian claims of territorial gains, noting a pattern of exaggeration by Russian military leadership. For example, on January 28, 2026, ISW explicitly refuted General Gerasimov’s claim of capturing Kupyansk-Uzlovaya and questioned the scale of advances in other areas, stating that Russian advances totaled 265.45 km² since January 1—less than half of the 500 km² claimed (Хартия 97, 2026-01-28). ISW relies on geolocated visual evidence, open-source intelligence, and frontline reporting to assess control, making its assessments more conservative and reliable than Russian military announcements. Given that the ultimate question hinges on ISW’s map showing Russian control of a specific intersection in Drobysheve, a formal ISW assessment indicating near-complete capture of the settlement would be a strong leading indicator that such a mapping update is imminent. As of late January 2026, ISW had not yet marked Drobysheve as under Russian control, suggesting that it requires high-confidence evidence before updating its assessments.

Sources:
- PravdaReport: https://pravadaily.com/russian-forces-take-17-settlements-as-gerasimov-visits-special-military-operation-zone/
- Хартия 97: https://charta97.org/en/2026/01/28/isw-gerasimov-has-been-lying-for-months/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-26, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) publishes a daily assessment or updates its interactive map narrative (on its official website or affiliated platforms) stating that Russian forces have captured over 95% of Drobysheve, including its central residential areas, based on geolocated evidence. The assessment must explicitly reference Drobysheve (Дробышеве) and provide visual or descriptive evidence of control over the majority of the settlement. 

The primary source for resolution is the ISW Ukraine Conflict Assessment page: https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/ukraine-conflict-assessment. If ISW’s website is unavailable, the DeepStateMap live update log (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used to verify corroborating evidence, provided it includes geolocated footage or frontline unit reports consistent with ISW’s evidentiary standards. If both sources are permanently unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of at least two credible conflict monitoring outlets (e.g., BBC Monitoring, Reuters, or The War Zone) reporting the same conclusion.

A statement from Russian military officials or pro-Russian sources alone is insufficient for resolution. The event must be documented by ISW or an equivalent independent, evidence-based source during the specified time window. If no such report is published by February 26, 2026, the question resolves No. Temporary glitches, unauthorized edits, or speculative social media claims do not count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a high-value early indicator for the ultimate question because ISW’s formal assessment of near-total capture of Drobysheve would strongly precede and predict a visual update on its map showing the specific intersection shaded red. Since ISW requires high-confidence geolocated evidence before updating its map—especially after past incidents of manipulation and misinformation—its public acknowledgment of effective Russian control over the vast majority of the settlement would signal that the threshold for mapping is likely to be met soon. Forecasters who disagree on whether Russia will capture the intersection by February 28 can use this subquestion to update their beliefs: a 'Yes' outcome would significantly increase confidence in the ultimate 'Yes' resolution, while a lack of such an assessment would suggest continued Ukrainian resistance or insufficient evidence, lowering the probability. Thus, this crux captures the evidentiary momentum required for the ultimate map change.

question: Will BTS release any tracks in 2025?

question: Will the Canberra Raiders win the 2025 National Rugby League?

subquestions.question: Will the Canberra Raiders qualify for the 2025 NRL Grand Final by winning their preliminary final between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-15?
subquestions.background_information:
The Canberra Raiders are one of the top contenders in the 2025 NRL season, having finished near the top of the ladder and securing home advantage in the finals series. According to the NRL finals structure, the top two teams at the end of the regular season earn the right to host a preliminary final if they win their qualifying final. The Raiders are aiming for their first premiership since 1994 and have shown strong home form in 2025, winning 8 of their last 9 games at GIO Stadium (Sporting News, 2025-07-27). The NRL confirmed that GIO Stadium is eligible to host a preliminary final, increasing the Raiders' chances of playing deep into the finals at home (Sporting News, 2025-07-21). subquestions.question: Will OpenAI announce a new marketplace or agent-based transaction feature in ChatGPT between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?

The agent can perform multi-step tasks such as research, form-filling, and data collection, and runs in a sandboxed environment with user controls like 'pause' and 'takeover' (SmashingApps.com). At the same time, OpenAI has been exploring new monetization models. While current revenue comes primarily from subscriptions (e.g., ChatGPT Plus, Team, Enterprise), the increasing autonomy of AI agents raises the possibility of transaction-based fees—such as charging a commission when an agent books a flight, completes a purchase, or refers a service. Such a model would align with broader industry trends, including Amazon’s use of AI agents in shopping and Google’s experimentation with AI-powered service bookings.

Recent reports indicate OpenAI is actively expanding its developer and enterprise integrations (The New Stack, 2025), including deep IDE integration via Codex and partnerships with platforms like GitHub and Google Workspace. These integrations increase the surface area for potential transactional use cases. However, as of August 31, 2025, there is no public evidence that OpenAI has implemented or announced a transaction fee model.

An announcement of a marketplace or agent-based transaction feature—such as an AI agent that can complete purchases, accept payments, or earn referral fees—would signal a strategic shift toward monetizing agent actions directly, rather than solely through subscriptions. Such a move would be a strong precursor to the implementation of transaction fees.

question: Trump Crypto Pardon Parlay
